jobs.title: Cloud Support Engineer
jobs.description:
Cloud Support Engineer

Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1100+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder led, profitable and growing.

We are hiring a Cloud Support Engineer to build a career with Canonical and support the technical needs of customers leveraging Ubuntu and open source products. If you have an affinity for open source development and a passion for technology, then you will enjoy working with some of the best people in the industry at Canonical.

While our engineers regularly solve deeply interesting, complex technical problems - from triaging cloud environments to root-cause analysis on unseen Linux kernel crashes - this is fundamentally a role rooted in human connection. You will act as a trusted peer and technical guide to external engineering teams, translating intricate open-source challenges into clear, empathetic solutions. We are rapidly expanding and looking for brilliant problem solvers who are just as passionate about building strong, collaborative relationships with customers as they are about the next generation of Canonical solutions.

Location: This is a globally remote role.

The role entails

  • Empathetic Engagement: Partner directly with customers across remote sessions, ticketing,, and live conversations to deeply understand and resolve their technical roadblocks.
  • Collaborative Problem Solving: Work hand-in-hand with internal engineering teams and regional peer groups to bridge the gap between complex code fixes and real-world customer satisfaction.
  • True Ownership: Manage your support cases with a strong sense of personal integrity, ensuring commitments are honored and customer expectations are communicated transparently and predictably.
  • Ubuntu Lifecycle Guidance: Develop a rich understanding of the Ubuntu development process, empowering you to give customers clear, human context regarding timelines for engineering fixes.
  • Knowledge Advocacy: Author and maintain accessible knowledge base articles, ensuring lessons learned are shared openly to elevate the entire open-source community.
  • Operational Reliability: Participate in a regular weekend working rotation to maintain seamless, high-touch continuity of care for our global partners.

What are we looking for in you

  • Communication Excellence: Exceptional written and spoken English, with a natural ability to convey technical complexity clearly, warmly, and compellingly.
  • The Soft-Skill Edge: A genuine passion for helping people, paired with the emotional intelligence to navigate high-stakes technical situations with composure and empathy.
  • Academic Dedication: Exceptional academic track record from both high school and university.
  • Educational Background: An undergraduate degree in a technical subject or a compelling narrative about your alternative chosen path.
  • Driven Mindset: A proven track record of going above-and-beyond expectations to deliver meaningful, outstanding results for teams or customers.
  • Linux & Cloud Familiarity: Practical, hands-on experience supporting Linux systems, with an exposure to three or more of the following:
    • Virtualization & Cloud: Using KVM or OpenStack.
    • Containers: primarily Docker, LXD/LXC, or Kubernetes.
    • Storage Ecosystems: Block, object, and network storage technologies.
    • System Networking: Navigating bonding, firewalls, bridging, switching, or MTU tuning.
  • Analytical Curiosity: A strong troubleshooting mindset—the ability to look into stack traces or logs, identify OS/application-level bugs, and strategically guide the customer through next steps.
  • Development Fundamentals: Basic programming logic in any language to help parse code and collaborate effectively with Canonical Engineering teams.

What we offer colleagues

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues
  • Priority Pass, and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since its inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

jobs.description:
Working Student (m/f/d)​Indexing Platform
Company Description

Since its creation in 2007 in the financial city of Frankfurt am Main, Solactive AG has grown to one of the key players in the indexing space. The German multi-asset index provider focusses on tailor-made indices, offering to its clients a faster service, with greater flexibility and at a reasonable cost. Solactive AG and its subsidiaries have become one of the fastest growing index providers over the past few years and support the leading investment banks and asset managers across the globe. We have gained global recognition for our role in the Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) industry, where we rank among the top providers worldwide for underlying indices. We also excel in diverse areas such as Structured Products and investment mandates, showcasing the wide range of our capabilities. The impact and value we bring to the market is palpable, but also in the reputation we have proudly built by being close to our customers, solidifying Solactive AG as a trusted and reliable ally in the ever-evolving global financial landscape.


Job Overview

Solactive's Aggregate team owns the intraday calculation of our indices: consuming live price streams, applying calculation logic across a wide range of indices, and producing a continuous output stream of index ticks throughout the trading day. The core platform is built in Java and engineered around throughput, latency, and correctness under concurrency, while custom business integrations are built in Python. As a Working Student you join a small team and contribute real, production-bound code to both, working alongside senior engineers who review your work and coach you.


Your Tasks

  • Implement well-scoped features and fixes in the Java calculation platform, such as improvements to calculation components, price stream consumption, or index tick production
  • Write unit, integration, and performance tests, including tests for concurrent code paths where ordering and timing matter
  • Help investigate correctness or performance issues: reproduce them, narrow them down, and propose fixes with senior guidance
  • Build and maintain Python integrations for business teams: connectors to the calculation platform, output adapters, validation checks, and small operational tools
  • Contribute to monitoring and developer tooling that makes calculation behaviour observable and easier to reason about
  • Take part in design and code reviews, ask questions, and document what you learn so the next person can pick it up faster


Your Profile

  • Enrolled student in computer science, software engineering, or a closely related field
  • Strong Java fundamentals: object-oriented design, collections, generics, and comfort reading and writing idiomatic modern Java
  • Solid grounding in core computer science: data structures, algorithms, and complexity, and in particular a working understanding of multithreading and concurrency (threads, synchronisation, memory visibility, races and deadlocks)
  • Openness to Python: no prior experience needed, but willingness to pick it up for integration and tooling work alongside Java
  • Familiarity with Git, the command line, and a testing mindset; interest in measuring performance rather than guessing at it
  • Ability to work independently on a scoped task, ask for help early when stuck, and communicate clearly in writing
  • Available for 15–20 hours per week during the semester, more during semester breaks
  • Interest in financial markets, market data, or index calculation is welcome but not required


Our Offer

  • Be part of the Solactive family  an international FinTech environment with flat hierarchies, real ownership, and strong growth opportunities.
  • Enjoy attractive benefits such as team events, Corporate Benefits access, a modern ergonomic office,free beverages and fruit.
  • Work on a real, high-impact production platform and contribute to architectural improvements not just feature tickets.
  • Gain hands-on experience with Java microservices, build systems, and dependency governance while collaborating with experienced engineers.
  • Build practical backend engineering skills that directly support your long-term career development.

jobs.title: Technician
jobs.description:
Technician

About Enact

The next defining technological breakthrough will be in the physical world. We stand at a historical inflection point: bringing general-purpose intelligence into robotics.

At Enact we rethink the entire robotic tech stack from model architectures and data pipelines, to the actuators and sensors that feed the model. Pushing beyond pure vision and language approaches, we build a proprioceptive nerve system, and the cortex that makes sense of it, to solve dexterity through whole-body force-awareness and deploy robots for thousands of tasks in industry and beyond.

We are shaping a company where brilliant and unconventional people thrive together on solving the hardest challenges of our time. We are truth seekers. We reason from first principles, test our beliefs against reality, and trust that the best ideas can come from anyone. We move fast. We care deeply about our work and colleagues and are driven by passion to change the status quo.

If this resonates, we're excited to hear from you.

In This Role

You will work closely with our hardware team to ensure high-quality, repeatable production of our actuators and robot systems. You will help make the hardware and process better through your feedback.

  • Mechanical Assembly, Manufacturing & Build Execution: You will be responsible for the mechanical build, assembly, and manufacturing steps of our robot systems

  • Fabrication & Prototyping Support: You will help produce custom parts (fixtures, jigs, and production parts) using manufacturing machines and 3D printers and feedback ways to improve/streamline the process.

  • In-Process Quality Control: You will perform systematic in-process QC against our quality metrics and log results to keep production traceable.

  • Machine Uptime and Maintenance: You will own the upkeep of our core machines and perform routine servicing, calibration and troubleshooting.

  • You will help grow the workshop itself: improving layout, tooling, and workflows as we scale.

What We're Looking For

  • Technical Skills: Hands-on mechanical assembly, comfort with workshop tools (calipers, soldering irons, power drills), 3D printing, and basic machine operation.

  • Technical Background: A relevant trade qualification (e.g., Polymechanic, Automation Technician, Electronics Technician, or similar apprenticeship) or equivalent hands-on experience in mechanical assembly, mechatronics, or electrical systems in a professional setting.

  • Problem Solving: The ability to troubleshoot hardware issues independently and critically analyze your own work to find improvements.

  • Reads engineering drawings fluently and works independently from written instructions

  • Attention to Detail: A preference for an organized, functional workspace and a systematic approach to technical tasks.

  • Fluent in English or in German but with at least basic English skills (A2/B1) and a willingness to learn (we are an international team)

Bonus Points If You

  • Have experience in mold-making or potting/encapsulation or electric motor production

  • Are a hands-on tinkerer and have built your own robots, RC planes, or custom 3D printers, or similar in your spare time. Send us pictures or a portfolio!

  • Have CAD drawing and prototyping experience

  • Have experience with heavy duty workshop tools like lathe, mill, CNC, etc.

What we offer

  • The opportunity to make a real impact working on some of the biggest challenges of our time

  • A fast-paced learning environment alongside an outstanding, driven team

  • Ownership from day one, with the ability to iterate quickly and see your impact firsthand in an early-stage startup

  • Visa sponsorship & relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

  • A world-class in-person setup in central Zürich, with excellent prototyping, robotics, and technical infrastructure for hands-on builders

  • Competitive compensation

jobs.title: Video Lead
jobs.description:
Video Lead

📈 Who We Are:

We are rebuilding the energy transaction, making it transparent and fair.

Our goal is to put power back where it belongs, in the hands of customers and to take on one of the most critical problems of our century, access to low cost electricity.

tem exists to fix a broken global energy market that’s long favoured legacy operators, intermediaries, and opaque pricing. Today’s electricity system was not designed for rapid decarbonisation, AI-driven efficiency or fair access for the actual users - businesses and generators.

We’ve built the first AI native transaction infrastructure to reinvent how electricity is bought, sold and priced. Our technology is designed to cut out the inefficient fees, automate complex market flows, and bring transparency and fairness to energy transactions at scale.

In late 2025, after extraordinary growth, we closed a $75 million Series B - led by Lightspeed Venture Partners with participation from Albion, Atomico, Allianz, Hitachi Ventures, Hitachi Ventures, Schroders Capital and others - positioning us for global expansion, deeper product innovation and category leadership.

We’re scaling internationally and building toward a future where AI-driven infrastructure is foundational to electricity markets worldwide.

Since launch, our modern utility product, known as RED, has already facilitated thousands of business customers and billions in energy transaction value, proving that modern software and AI can transform an industry built on legacy systems.

At tem, we’re not just building another energy company, we’re rearchitecting market infrastructure so that transparency, efficiency and sustainability become the default, not the exception.

In short

We're looking for a Video Lead to shoot and edit for tem. Full-time, £70,000, based anywhere in the UK with shoots around the country.

tem connects businesses directly with the renewable generators that power them, which makes it an unusually diverse thing to film: solar and wind sites, the people who run them, the businesses buying from them, and the engineers building the technology in between. Here's some of what we've made so far: here, here, here and here.

The work we want to make

Two kinds of video, held to the same standard.

Considered films, where pacing, sound and framing carry the story and every shot is there for a reason. The kind someone who has never thought about energy watches to the end, because they've started to care about the person in it.

And social pieces that aren't templates: short cuts made with real intent, where the rhythm, timing, sound design and effects all serve the idea. Native to the platform, unmistakably crafted.

You'll move between the two in the same week without either one slipping.

If you're freelance - most of the best shooter-editors work for themselves, and we understand why. Here's what we'd want you to know.

This isn't corporate video. Generator stories, customer films, policy explainers, engineering pieces and people-led series - a social series one week, a customer film the next. When it's worth moving fast, we can go from idea to published within a week, if that’s what we collectively decide.

You'd be building something, not borrowing it. Rather than picking up someone else's style for a few weeks, you'd shape what tem's video looks and feels like, and build a body of work around it over years. You're expected, and encouraged, to argue when you see a better way.

Fewer feedback rounds. One brand, one small team, and a direct line to whoever wrote the brief. You learn tem once, properly.

The money. £70,000, stock options, paid holiday, and no invoices to chase or quiet months to plan around.

What you'll own

tem's video from first shot to final export: how it's planned, shot and cut, and how it looks and sounds across everything we publish. You'll sit in the Brand team and report into the Content Lead.

  • Shoots. Planning properly - schedule, kit, shot list, a recce where it's worth it - then staying alert on the day for what the plan couldn't know. Running most shoots solo, and knowing when a piece needs extra crew and when a phone and good instincts will do.

  • People. Most of the generators, engineers and finance directors you'll film have never been on camera. Putting them at ease and getting the real version of them is half the job.

  • The edit (around 70% of your week). Cutting, grading, mixing and titling in Premiere Pro. Giving short social pieces the same care as the long ones, letting the considered films breathe, and making something good from very little when there's no shoot.

  • Story and style. Turning a brief or rough idea into how it should be shot and sequenced, pushing back when you see a better version, and developing a visual language for tem video over time.

How we use AI (and how we don't)

We're not looking for someone to make AI-generated films - our content works because it's real. We use tools where they earn their place: transcription and paper edits, selects, audio clean-up, subtitles, cutdowns and versioning, the occasional fix in post, and pre-production like moodboards and storyboards. We want someone curious enough to try new tools, with the judgement to know when not to.

What we're looking for

Must haves

  • A portfolio, wherever it lives, that shows both halves: considered, human storytelling and social work cut with real intent.

Bonus points

What you get

  • Your say in what video kit we invest in for the content team.

  • Remote first and flexible working, with no internal meetings on Friday afternoons.

How to apply

jobs.description:
Quality Manager

About EHG

EH Group (EHG) is a rapidly growing fuel cell power platform delivering onsite power to AI data centers, defense, and industry. Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide.

Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.

The opportunity

We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.

You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.

Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.

Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

What you'll own

  • One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

  • Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

  • In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

  • Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

  • Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

  • Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

  • Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

  • Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

  • Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

  • Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

What we're looking for

Core experience

  • Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.

  • Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.

  • Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.

  • Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.

  • Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.

  • Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.

  • The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.

  • Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.

Especially compelling

  • Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.

  • Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes.

  • Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end.

  • Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators.

  • Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth.

  • Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required.

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you.

  • Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.

  • The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth.

Note: Swiss work authorization or eligibility is required for this role, along with the ability to travel to the United States.

Strategic Account Executive - French Speaking

About HappyRobot

HappyRobot is the infrastructure for enterprises to build and orchestrate AI workforces. Our AI workers don't just communicate through voice and email - they make decisions, take action, and run operations autonomously across entire enterprise systems. Born in Y Combinator (S23) and backed by a16z, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo with over $150M raised, we power critical operations for global enterprises worldwide.

Our platform is battle-tested in the most demanding environments, where AI has real consequences. We started in logistics, built our own voice stack, models, and orchestration layer from the ground up, and are now bringing that infrastructure to every enterprise that runs the real economy. Learn more about our vision in our manifesto.

 

Role Overview

We are looking for a highly driven Strategic Account Executive to join our growing sales team. In this role, you will be responsible for managing the full sales cycle, building strong relationships with enterprise clients, and driving revenue growth.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Enterprise Sales Execution - Own the full sales cycle from prospecting to closing enterprise-level deals.

  • Pipeline Management - Develop and maintain a robust pipeline of enterprise accounts, ensuring consistent deal flow.

  • Consultative Selling - Understand client challenges, industry trends, and business goals to position our SaaS solution effectively.

  • Relationship Building - Establish and nurture long-term relationships with key stakeholders and decision-makers.

  • Strategic Negotiations - Lead complex negotiations, ensuring a win-win outcome for both the client and the company.

  • Cross-functional Collaboration - Work closely with Sales Engineering, Customer Success, and Product teams to deliver tailored solutions.

  • Revenue Growth - Meet and exceed sales targets, contributing to the company's overall revenue goals.

  • Market Insights - Stay informed about industry trends, competitor activity, and market shifts to refine sales strategies.

 

Must have

  • Experience in enterprise sales, preferably in the SaaS industry.

  • Proven track record of consistently meeting or exceeding sales quotas in a B2B environment.

  • Large ACV track record

  • Strong experience managing complex sales cycles and working with multiple stakeholders.

  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills.

  • Ability to analyze customer needs and align them with the right solutions.

  • Experience with CRM tools such as Salesforce, HubSpot, or similar platforms.

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

 

Why join us?

  • Join a world-class team of engineers and builders.

  • Backed by top investors including a16z, Y Combinator, Base10, Prysm Capital and Eurazeo.

  • Have ownership and autonomy of projects and are encouraged to ship.

  • Comprehensive Benefits including healthcare, dental, vision coverage.

  • Competitive salary + equity in a high-growth startup.

Our Operating Principles


Extreme Ownership

We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.

Craftsmanship

Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. Whether it’s a product feature, an internal doc, or a sales call — we treat it as a reflection of our standards. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

We are “majos”
Be friendly & have fun with your coworkers. Always be genuine & honest, but kind. “Majo” is our way of saying: be a good human. Be approachable, helpful, and warm. We’re building something ambitious, and it’s easier (and more fun) when we enjoy the ride together. We give feedback with kindness, challenge each other with respect, and celebrate wins together without ego.

Urgency with Focus
Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. We’re running a high-speed marathon — not a sprint with no strategy.

Talent Density and Meritocracy
Hire only people who can raise the average; ‘exceptional performance is the passing grade.’ Ability trumps seniority. We believe the best teams are built on talent density — every hire should raise the bar. We reward contribution, not titles or tenure. We give ownership to those who earn it, and we all hold each other to a high standard. A-players want to work with other A-players — that’s how we win.

First-Principles Thinking
Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. We go back to basics, ask why things are the way they are, and rebuild from the ground up if needed. This mindset pushes us to innovate, challenge stale assumptions, and move faster than incumbents. It’s how we build what others think is impossible.

jobs.title: Composite Technician - Airframe
jobs.description:
Composite Technician - Airframe

About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the role

As the composite technician on the Airframe team, your core mission is to prototype carbon structures fast, in-house — from mould to finished, quality-checked part — and to bring innovative solutions that make assembly and prototyping easier. A true hands-on professional, you combine technical skills, initiative, and a maker mindset. You build tooling, lay up and finish composite parts (carbon / glass fibre), and turn the engineers' CAD into flight-worthy structures on short cycles. You are also the owner of technical drawings and supplier quotations for the parts you handle, and the one who trains production operators when a design moves to series. You thrive with minimal supervision, favour pragmatic, quick-result approaches over perfect-but-slow tooling, and are equally comfortable laying up a part, machining or printing a mould, and reading a technical drawing.

Technical skills

Key responsibilities

Rapid in-house prototyping (core)

  • Produce carbon prototype structures quickly in-house, choosing the fastest viable route rather than heavy tooling when a proto is the goal.

  • Propose innovative, simple solutions to speed up assembly and prototyping.

  • Design certain parts and prototyping tools yourself (fixtures, adapters, simple structural parts) when it is faster than going through the design loop.

  • Iterate fast with the design engineers: short loops between concept, part and feedback, flagging manufacturability issues before they cost a mould.

Tooling & moulds

  • Build and maintain moulds and tooling, in coordination with the design team; machine or 3D-print mould masters, prepare and polish mould surfaces.

  • Design and build layup jigs, trimming templates, bonding and assembly fixtures.

  • Manage the composite workshop consumables and material inventory (fabrics, resins, cores, vacuum consumables) including storage and shelf-life follow-up.

Design & documentation

  • Read and interpret 2D/3D drawings and ply books; model simple parts and tooling in CAD when needed; give manufacturability feedback early.

  • Own the technical drawings: produce and keep up to date the manufacturing drawings for the parts and tooling you handle.

  • Write and maintain clear, accessible fabrication procedures, ply books and cure logs on Confluence so processes are repeatable by others.

  • Optimise part designs for their manufacturing process: adapt geometries for plastic injection (wall thickness, draft angles, ribs) or for composite / 3D-printed fabrication (layup feasibility, demoulding, printability), in collaboration with the design engineers.

Support & improvement

  • Support assembly and mechanical testing, including preparing test coupons and samples for structural analysis.

  • Identify and propose process and quality improvements; help run the composite workshop safely (dust extraction, PPE, resin handling and waste management).

  • Own the knowledge transfer to production: train the production operators on fabrication and assembly processes, and validate that a process is repeatable by others before handover.

Candidate profile

  • Technical diploma or degree in composite materials, mechanical / aerospace manufacturing, industrial technology, or equivalent hands-on experience.

  • Proven experience in rapid in-house composite prototyping (carbon / glass fibre): hand layup, vacuum bagging, infusion and/or prepreg; mould making and surface preparation a strong plus.

  • Track record of quick, pragmatic solutions — getting a functional carbon part out fast, with sound trade-offs, rather than perfect parts requiring heavy tooling.

  • Ability to read technical drawings and ply books, and to control layup orientation, resin ratios, debulking and cure cycles with rigour and traceability.

🐙 Kraken Generation Flex

The energy industry is undergoing the largest transformation since industrialisation, at an unprecedented rate of change and we are positioning ourselves at the heart of it. In the UK, with a legally binding Net Zero target for 2050 and a clean-power ambition for 2030, we are scaling rapidly to integrate Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into the grid.

Kraken is recognised as a thought leader and innovator. With complete independence from Octopus Energy, we are building a SaaS business that digitally connects hundreds of thousands of DERs with energy markets. As our UK fleet grows and we support our expansion across Europe, we are looking for an Integrations Engineer to help turn customer sites into market-connected, controllable assets.

🏠 Where you’ll fit in and role summary

As we scale our fleet of integrated assets, we are looking for an Electrical Engineer to support the delivery of our site integrations and grow into owning them, learning the full lifecycle from the early information stage through design, deployment and testing.

You’ll be part of an engineering delivery team, based in Manchester, who take an integration project from the very early information stage, design how it will be integrated into Kraken’s platform and then turn that design into a live, controllable, market-participating asset.

Engineering delivery is an innovative and engineering-focused team with a culture that fosters collaboration and fresh thinking to create a new energy system. Alongside design, deployment and testing; they constantly look into ways to improve efficiency through tooling and the automation of repetitive tasks. They collaborate daily with delivery managers and customer success to onboard new sites as well as support the existing.

🚀 What you'll own

  • Integration design contribution: With guidance, analyse provided information and contribute to hardware and software integration approaches. When necessary, exchange information with customer technical representatives through meetings and emails, and take part in design discussions with other team members.

  • Developing domain knowledge: Build up your knowledge in one or more technical areas. This could include grid regulations (G99, G100, Grid Code etc.), energy markets, multi BMUs, industrial communication protocols, industrial networking, internet of things, cyber security and so on.

Understand the requirements for an integration and judge if the gateway software is able to support it or will need new development work. The team will help you get gateway configuration literate and you will carry out deployments and changes independently over time.

  • Hardware and Software Deployments: Learn the process of our hardware and software deployments. Over time, take ownership of the configuration, deployment and testing with guidance from the senior engineers.

  • Networking and cyber security: Contribute to hardware and network connectivity designs, keeping our own cyber security posture in mind as well as addressing the concerns from customers, with the support of the internal security team.

  • Site testing & commissioning: Carry out site testing and commissioning initially with the support of the team and building toward doing this independently as onboarding demand grows.

  • Incidents & compliance: Help address engineering help requests from other teams and support incident response in the case of issues at existing sites.

🧠 What you'll bring to the party

  • Understanding of the Regulations: Working knowledge of the UK Grid Code, G99 and the other obligations of a grid-connected asset before it can participate in the energy markets.

  • Understanding of the UK Energy Markets: Working understanding of the NESO ancillary services (Dynamic Containment / Moderation / Regulation, Firm Frequency Response), the Balancing Mechanism, and the DNO connection/integration process.

  • Technical judgement: Sound technical judgement and a structured approach to problems, working with the team to agree and implement a solution.

  • Power plant systems: Ability to read and analyse single line diagrams for a given power plant to understand the site architecture for the points of metering and control instrumentation.

  • Asset integration: Exposure to, or a keen interest in, integrating BESS (grid-scale and/or C&I) and/or RES (Wind and Solar) for telemetry and control.

  • Integration design: Ability to contribute to clear integration designs and design documentation.

  • Hardware and Networking: Familiarity with control systems deployments and their connectivity including the local networking and cyber security aspects, and an ability to help debug site connectivity and networking issues (including 4G routers and firewalls) with support.

  • Industrial Communication Protocols: Practical experience or a good working knowledge of Modbus (TCP/RTU); awareness of one or more of IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61400-25, OPC-UA or DNP3 is a plus.

  • CAD, Diagrams and Tools: Experience or familiarity with CAD tools such as AutoCAD or BricsCAD, Miro and Notion.

  • Communication: A clear communicator who documents their work (e.g. in design docs and Notion) and collaborates well with the team.

  • Commissioning landscape: Awareness of the other parties involved in site commissioning for power plants, their roles and responsibilities, and how we work with them.

  • Engineering background: Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering, Automation/Control, Software, or a related field - or equivalent practical experience in industrial/energy integration.

  • A proactive and collaborative mindset: You are eager to learn and grow, reliable and collaborative. You take initiative, communicate openly, raise risks early, and care about safe working. You welcome feedback, support your teammates, and steadily build toward taking on more independent ownership of integrations over time.

  • Travel: Willingness to travel to customers and sites although travel is very occasional. Awareness of site safety is required as we may work with site personnel even though we are remote.

⭐️ Bonus points

  • Wider knowledge of grid compliance (G99, G100, Grid Code) and where the Kraken system fits in.

  • Experience with AWS IoT Greengrass or similar edge-deployment architectures.

  • Familiarity with software/scripting and templating (e.g. Python, Rust, the Linux command line) and Git-based workflows.

  • Understanding of IT/OT security in the energy sector (IEC 62443, NIS Regulations awareness).

  • Exposure to wider European balancing markets / ENTSO-E frameworks and TSO integrations.

jobs.description:
Software Engineer, Perception & Vision

Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

The Role

As a Computer Vision Engineer, you will build and own the perception systems behind our multi-sensor surveillance and robotics stack. This is a builder's role first: you start from the best available models, off-the-shelf where they do the job and trained in-house where they don't, and turn them into reliable, real-time systems that detect, track, and re-identify objects across cameras and run efficiently on edge hardware. We care less about novel papers and more about whether what you build works on a live site and stays working.

What You'll Work On

  • Design and ship cross-camera object re-identification (ReID) for people and vehicles across distributed camera networks, in all light and environmental conditions.

  • Build high-throughput object detection and multi-object tracking pipelines that run across many simultaneous video streams.

  • Integrate and adapt vision-language models (VLMs) for open-vocabulary detection, scene understanding, and operator-facing situational awareness.

  • Own the video ingestion and streaming path (RTSP, WebRTC) from camera to model, with attention to latency, resilience, and dropped-frame handling.

  • Optimize and deploy models on edge hardware: TensorRT, quantization (INT8/FP16), pruning, and other techniques to hit real-time targets on Jetson and edge-class devices.

  • Evaluate, fine-tune, and integrate existing open-source and commercial models, and train custom models when off-the-shelf options fall short, knowing when each is the right call.

  • Work closely with the software and robotics teams so perception output feeds downstream autonomy and alerting.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for a strong engineer who has shipped computer vision or ML systems into production, ideally in an embodied, multi-camera, or multi-modal setting. You think rigorously about data, evaluation, and where models break under real-world constraints. You're happy taking an existing state-of-the-art model and doing the unglamorous work of making it fast, reliable, and deployable on hardware, and equally happy training your own when nothing off-the-shelf fits. You measure success by whether the system works on a live site, not by novelty.

Your Background:

  • Proven track record building and shipping computer vision or ML systems in production (3+ years or equivalent depth).

  • Strong understanding of SOTA techniques for cross-camera ReID, object detection, and multi-object tracking.

  • Hands-on experience with VLMs, and a working grasp of the current model landscape.

  • Solid grasp of real-time video streaming (RTSP, WebRTC) and the realities of multi-stream pipelines.

  • Experience taking models from prototype to deployment on edge hardware: TensorRT, quantization, latency tuning.

  • Strong Python and PyTorch (or JAX) skills, with a systems-builder mindset: you ship working systems, building on SOTA and training your own when needed.

  • Broad ML literacy beyond vision, and solid software engineering hygiene: version control, reproducibility, evaluation discipline.

  • Strong data pipeline skills: curating, cleaning, labelling, and managing large image and video datasets.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience with NVIDIA DeepStream.

  • MLOps experience: model versioning, CI/CD for ML, monitoring deployed models in the field.

  • Familiarity with RAG and LLM-based pipelines, and integrating them into a wider system.

  • Background in surveillance, robotics, or safety-critical / defence systems, including on-prem or air-gapped deployment.

  • Publications at top venues (ICCV, CVPR, ICLR, NeurIPS) are a plus but not expected. We value shipped systems more.

What We Offer

  • Ownership: you are the first in line to build and lead the team you help hire.

  • Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

  • Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

  • Culture: a small, international founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

What this role actually is

This is a hands-on operational role. Your customers are our employees. The work is a mix of live support, access administration, endpoint and MDM management, onboarding and offboarding, equipment logistics, and documentation, plus improving those processes so the same problems stop coming back.

You will own requests end-to-end rather than passing them along, work directly with non-technical colleagues, and handle several things at once on a busy day. Routine service work is a permanent part of the job, not a temporary phase before something else.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own employee IT requests end-to-end: prioritize by impact and urgency, keep people informed, resolve, document, and prevent recurrence.

  • Administer user accounts, permissions, and access across Google Workspace, Atlassian, GitHub, and AWS, applying least privilege.

  • Run IT onboarding and offboarding: accounts provisioned on day one, access revoked promptly on exit, devices recovered.

  • Prepare, configure, and maintain macOS and Windows workstations through MDM: policies, software deployment, patching, encryption, and recovery.

  • Own IT equipment procurement, delivery, returns, and inventory accuracy for employees across supported locations, including international shipping and vendor coordination.

  • Troubleshoot hardware, software, network, and SaaS issues methodically: reproduce, isolate, verify.

  • Maintain IT documentation, knowledge-base articles, and asset records so support does not depend on one person being online.

  • Reduce repetitive work through practical scripting and automation, and improve support processes without weakening security controls.

  • Enforce IT security and access policies; recognize and escalate suspicious activity and access gaps.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience in IT support, Service Desk, or system administration, with personal ownership of the areas above (not adjacent exposure while other teams handled them).

  • Practical experience supporting macOS in a production employee environment.

  • Hands-on MDM administration (Jamf, Kandji, Intune, JumpCloud, Hexnode, or similar): enrollment, policies, software deployment, compliance.

  • Administration of Google Workspace, plus at least two of: Atlassian, GitHub access management, or cloud IAM (AWS / GCP / Azure).

  • Demonstrated ownership of access lifecycle - joiners, movers, leavers - including approval flows and least-privilege practice.

  • Experience with equipment provisioning, inventory, and remote/international delivery.

  • Solid understanding of network fundamentals (DNS, DHCP, VPN, TCP/IP) and endpoint security basics (encryption, EDR, MFA/SSO).

  • Experience working in a ticketing system with SLAs, and maintaining written documentation.

  • Ability to handle a high volume of concurrent requests, interruptions, and difficult support situations while communicating calmly and clearly.

  • At least one concrete example of automating or redesigning a repetitive support process, where you can explain your own contribution and the measurable outcome.

  • Ukrainian: fluent. English: B1 or higher — enough to support colleagues, write tickets, and maintain documentation in an international company.

Nice to Have

  • Scripting and automation (Bash, PowerShell, Python).

  • Apple Business Manager, Zero-Touch / automated device deployment.

  • Experience with VPN, LDAP, or ZTNA solutions.

  • Exposure to ISO 27001 / SOC 2 processes or security audits.

  • Interest in security topics (access control, endpoint security, Zero Trust).

  • iGaming industry experience.

  • Relevant certifications (CompTIA A+/Network+, Google Workspace, Microsoft, Apple, or similar).

Customer Success Lead
jobs.description:
Customer Success Lead

💬 Accurx is solving healthcare productivity for the NHS.

For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. At Accurx, we’re changing that by building a single, system-wide platform that helps every patient get gold-standard, efficient, and joined-up care.

What started as a way for GPs to text a patient has now evolved into an all-in-one digital toolkit used by 98% of GP practices.

Our platform now powers Total Triage to manage patient demand, and Self-Book, which lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with Patient Questionnaires for long-term conditions, while Accumail finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with Accurx Scribe, our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time.

We’re not just shipping features. We’re giving clinicians their time back and ensuring every patient journey is as smooth as it should be.

That sounds cool - what does a Customer Success Lead have to do with it?

Accurx works with 41 of the 42 NHS ICBs and is growing fast in secondary care. To keep up with how the NHS is organising itself, our Account Management team has just moved to a regional model, with leads for London, the South and the North. The goal is simple: join up what we’re learning across primary care, secondary care, acute, community and mental health, and make sure the best opportunities get surfaced across the whole of England, not just in one set of ICBs.

We’re hiring a Customer Success Lead for the North. You’ll lead a team of Customer Success Managers across primary and secondary care and be the strategic, zoomed-out view of the region. Your team is close to the accounts. Your job is to spot the patterns across them, turn what they’re hearing into strategy, and help Accurx show up at a regional level.

The challenges you’ll solve as a Customer Success Lead

  • Lead and grow a team of CSMs. You’ll start with three CSMs, each with their own region, customers and stage of the customer journey. You’ll coach them, unblock them and help them do the best work of their careers.

  • Bring two very different care settings together. Primary care is about deepening trust we’ve built over years. Secondary care is about firsts: new services, longer implementations and goalposts that move. You’ll work out what connects them, what doesn’t, and where learnings from one can speed up the other.

  • Turn insight into strategy. Your team will feed you what’s happening on the ground. You’ll spot trends, gaps and duplicated effort across the region and turn them into projects, goals and growth opportunities in products like Accurx Scribe and Total Triage.

  • Own the commercial picture for your region. You’ll keep a close eye on churn, risk, renewals and upsell across your team’s accounts, and represent the region at our weekly business reviews with the exec team.

  • Build the playbook with your fellow leads. The regional model is brand new. Alongside the leads for London and the South, you’ll shape how we work, what best practice looks like and how we scale it.

  • Be the link across the business. You’ll work closely with implementation, transformation, support and business development, making sure the voice of our customers shapes where Accurx goes next.


You should apply if...

  • You’ve led customer-facing teams. You have a few years of people management in customer success or account management, and you love helping others grow.

  • You’ve built things from the ground up. You’ve been on a startup to scale-up journey, worn a lot of hats, and taken customers from never having heard of you to being your biggest advocates.

  • You care about depth, not volume. You’ve looked after long-standing, strategic relationships rather than a high-volume queue, and you know that trust is what makes customers stick.

  • You can zoom out. You don’t need to be in the weeds of every account. You’re great at spotting patterns, asking the right questions and knowing where your team needs you most.

  • You’re comfortable with ambiguity. You’re happy to try something, get it wrong, learn and go again. Process is something you create, not something you wait for.

  • You’re a big collaborator. You’re an incredible communicator and listener, and you know the best outcomes come from working across teams.

  • You’re curious about the NHS. Healthcare experience is welcome but not essential. What matters is empathy for the pressure the NHS is under and the patience to build trust in a complex system.


What’s in it for me?

You’ll be joining an established but fast-growing Tech for Good movement, where we’re led by our Principles and our mission to Solve Healthcare Productivity.

  • £70,000 - £90,000 salary + share options up to £30,000

  • Benefits to suit you: adjust your healthcare cover, your pension or life insurance, whatever stage you’re at in life

  • Flexible Working: We are an office-first culture and ask that you’re in our (dog-friendly) Shoreditch office 3 days a week, with core hours of 10am-4pm

  • Time off: You’ll get 28 days of holiday (plus bank holidays) and up to 4 weeks to work from anywhere per year

  • Family matters: We offer enhanced parental leave, fertility support and parental loss support

  • We have our very own Chef! Free healthy breakfasts, snacks and lunches will be provided, with the occasional sweet treat!

Want to know more about the company or the hiring process? Check out our Careers page and Candidate hub.

Find us across social media: Medium, LinkedIn, X, Instagram and YouTube.

Diversity and Equal Opportunities: We are an equal opportunities employer and a pleasant and supportive place to work. Help us use technology to make a big green dent in the universe!

Kraken powers some of the most innovative global developments in energy.

By optimising renewable generation, building a more intelligent grid, and empowering utilities to deliver an exceptional customer experience, our operating system is transforming the industry worldwide.

It’s an incredibly exciting time to work in energy. Join us on our mission to improve the lives of ONE BILLION humans within the decade and shape a cleaner, better future for everyone.

🏡 Where you'll fit in:
KrakenFlex is the flexibility arm of the Kraken group, built to put a big green dent in global carbon emissions by rewriting how electricity grids operate. We stabilize the grid and help renewables come online much faster by managing the second-by-second balance of clean power. Right now, our platform connects nearly one million assets worldwide, putting over 6GW of live load under our direct control.

Behind the scenes, that means handling massive technical scale: solving complex optimization problems in real time and processing 15 billion data readings a day from the latest green technologies, ensuring the grid stays reliable without relying on old fossil-fuel backup plants.

The next phase of our journey involves monumental growth. Currently operational across multiple countries, we are poised for further global expansion, scaling our asset base and tackling unique grid challenges in new territories. Our mission is to integrate an increasingly diverse array of green flexibility assets while ensuring our market-leading platform remains exceptionally stable and performant.

What is Optimisation in Flex?
The Optimisation chapter is the mathematical and algorithmic engine of the KrakenFlex platform. While other chapters manage physical asset connectivity or ingest market signals, this domain is responsible for the intelligence that decides exactly what every asset should do, second by second, to maximise both grid stability and financial returns.

The teams within this chapter build and maintain the real-time dispatch engines, predictive forecasting models, and algorithmic solvers that handle massive multi-asset portfolios. This involves translating complex market rules, physical asset constraints (like battery degradation curves, state-of-charge limits, and ramp rates), and fluctuating price signals into optimised execution strategies.

The defining challenge for this chapter is scaling computational performance alongside our rapid asset growth. Running complex, multi-variable mathematical models in tight real-time windows requires immense efficiency. The core tension lies in balancing the demand from data science and quantitative engineering to introduce increasingly sophisticated models with the strict platform requirement for absolute reliability, low latency, and cost-effective cloud compute.

Ultimately, this chapter must move away from bespoke optimisation routines tailored to individual markets or asset types. Your goal is to architect a highly performant, modular optimisation core that uses standard abstract layers, allowing us to roll out new algorithms or expand into new global territories without rewriting the underlying engine.

🚀 What you’ll own:
The Flex platform is built on autonomous Chapters, which are collections of specialists focused on delivering a core service or business outcome, defined by the unchanging nature of the energy business (independent of technology, hardware, or regional differences). A Head of Engineering leading a Chapter is a senior leadership role combining strong product thinking, engineering judgement, operational awareness, and people leadership. They manage managers and senior individual contributors, helping teams own their product surfaces, make sound trade-offs, and deliver reliably.

This role requires influencing beyond its formal remit, spotting cross-team patterns, clarifying ownership and decision-making, and driving initiatives to turn recurring issues into visible actions with owners, dates, and measures of success. Ultimately, they maintain the technical vision for their specific area, ensuring services are appropriately owned, maintained, and aligned with Flex's sustainable growth.

  • Managing the leads.

  • Ensuring the services in that area are owned and maintained appropriately.

  • Ensuring the appropriate level of quality and resilience, with a specific focus on reducing system incidents and improving stability.

  • Ensuring appropriate tech debt is prioritised to support sustainable delivery.

🧠 What you’ll bring to the party:

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Our system runs on-prem at industrial facilities, critical infrastructure, and military sites, integrated with the cameras, networks, and robots already in place. You survey the site, plan the deployment, install and integrate the system, tune it to the site's conditions, and hand it over to operators who will rely on it daily.

You are also the technical face of Laelaps on site. You work with security operators to understand how they actually work and where the bottlenecks are, align with their leadership on what success looks like, and translate what you learn into configuration, code, and product priorities. Early deployments you run alongside the founders; over time you own sites and accounts independently.

Expect roughly half your time at customer sites in Switzerland and Europe, and the rest in Zurich, turning field lessons into tooling and automation that make each deployment faster than the last. This is an engineering role with a customer in the room, not a support or services role.

What You'll Own

  • Deployments end-to-end: site surveys, network and hardware planning, installation, camera and VMS integration, commissioning, validation, and handover.

  • On-prem infrastructure: install and manage our stack on edge hardware (NVIDIA DGX Spark, Jetson Thor class devices) inside customer networks, often air-gapped or heavily restricted.

  • Integrations: connect existing cameras, sensors, VMS platforms, and robots into one coordinated system, and write the glue code where no integration exists yet.

  • System tuning: calibrate detection and tracking to each site's terrain, lighting, and threat profile until the system performs in the field as it does in the demo.

  • Pilots to production: make POCs succeed technically, because pilots that work become contracts.

  • Customer understanding: sit with operators, interview stakeholders from the control room to the leadership floor, and map the real problems and bottlenecks behind the stated requirements.

  • Customer trust: train operators, respond fast when something breaks, and be the engineer customers ask for by name.

  • The deployment playbook: turn every hard-won lesson into runbooks, tooling, and automation that compound.

  • Product feedback: bring real field signal back to the core engineering team and shape the roadmap with it.

Who We're Looking For

We are looking for an engineer who runs toward the messy parts, with the EQ to match the IQ. You are as comfortable in a server room or on a windswept perimeter as you are in a terminal, and just as comfortable in a conversation. You can spend a shift with a security operator and earn enough trust that they tell you what actually goes wrong at 3 a.m., then brief a head of security or a site director in their language, not yours. You listen more than you pitch, you read the room, and you switch registers between the guard house and the boardroom without breaking stride. You debug across the whole stack without ceremony: is it the hardware, the network, the driver, the model, or the config? Above all, you take personal ownership of the outcome: the deployment works because you made it work, and the customer trusts us because you earned it.

Your Background

The next defining technological breakthrough will be in the physical world. We stand at a historical inflection point: bringing general-purpose intelligence into robotics.

jobs.title: Technical Support Specialist , UK
jobs.description:
Technical Support Specialist , UK

Nash is looking for a Technical Support Specialist to join our global, 24/7 Technical Support team. This role sits at the heart of how Nash stabilizes the platform for our enterprise merchants - owning the investigation, resolution, and clean escalation of complex platform and integration issues across our delivery orchestration system.

Technical Support is Nash's intake and stabilization layer for everything beyond high-volume delivery inquiries. You'll be the person customers and internal teams rely on when something unusual is happening on the platform: a stuck integration, an unexpected provider behavior, a configuration question that needs real investigation. You'll resolve what you can, escalate what you can't with the context needed to move quickly, and help build the knowledge base that makes the next occurrence faster.

This is a role for someone who enjoys the detective work of complex, ambiguous technical problems, communicates clearly under pressure, and takes ownership seriously.

LOCATION

Remote in UK (required)

UK Time (GMT / BST): Thursday - Monday, 9A - 6P

TRAINING

4 weeks, Monday - Friday

A note on location

This is a remote role, but candidates must be located in the UK. This is a hard requirement driven by contractual data access obligations with our enterprise customers, not a preference - we are not able to make exceptions.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

  • Platform and integration investigation. Diagnose configuration questions, known error patterns, API and webhook issues, and account-specific behavior across the Nash platform.

  • Escalation quality. When an issue needs Engineering or Enterprise Operations, you own the handoff — clear reproduction steps, investigation performed, impact assessment, and severity. Escalations from this team are expected to be actionable on arrival.

  • Incident coordination. Serve as the active shift team for P1 incidents — coordinating communication, engaging Engineering immediately, and keeping customers and internal stakeholders informed through resolution.

  • Proactive monitoring. Watch Datadog dashboards, alerts, and logs for anomalies and emerging risks. Surface issues before they become customer-impacting where possible.

  • Knowledge base contribution. Document resolution patterns for novel issues so the next occurrence becomes a known pattern. Your work directly reduces future escalation volume.

  • Overflow support. Act as overflow for Delivery Support during peak windows when issues exceed their scope.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 5 - 6+ years in Technical Support, Support Engineering, or a related technical role in a SaaS environment

  • Hands-on experience investigating complex platform issues - not just routing tickets, but actually diagnosing what is happening

  • Comfort with APIs, webhooks, and integration troubleshooting in a production environment

  • Experience with monitoring and observability tools (Datadog, New Relic, Grafana, or similar)

  • Clear, calm written communication — especially during incidents or when customers are frustrated

  • Judgment about when to investigate further versus escalate, and the discipline to document thoroughly either way

  • Located in UK (remote)

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience supporting logistics, marketplace, or high-volume transactional platforms

  • Prior incident response or post-mortem participation

  • Experience contributing to knowledge bases or support documentation that actually gets used

  • Familiarity with ticketing platforms like Pylon, Zendesk, or similar

More about Nash

Nash is the platform that powers modern logistics.

Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line.

Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion.

We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it.

Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco.

What You’ll Love About Us

✅ Early-stage, well-funded startup – directly impact the company and grow your career!
✅ Quarterly broader team on-sites to bond with teammates
✅ Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity
✅ Flexible paid time off
✅ Health, dental, and vision insurance

Operating across the entire customer and merchant lifecycle, we tackle a diverse array of challenges, from optimizing checkout conversion and mitigating fraud risk to building scalable data foundations and enabling international growth. We analyze performance not just to report on it, but to determine where to invest resources for maximum impact through building tools, scalable data infrastructure, and analytical frameworks.

We improve the analytics experience across Affirm by streamlining workflows and fostering a culture of learning and documentation. By taking ownership of the entire analytical lifecycle, from initial question to final business decision, we turn complex data and systems into clear, actionable signals that ensure Affirm grows efficiently and intelligently.

One Role, Multiple Teams

We are hiring multiple Analyst I roles across Affirm's Risk & Analytics organization through this single job posting. Rather than interviewing for one specific team, candidates will go through a shared interview process designed to assess the core skills we look for across R&A.

If selected, we will work with you to determine the best team match based on your interests, experience, strengths, and current business needs. You will have the opportunity to learn more about our teams and share your preferences as you move through the process.

Potential team placements include:

  • Point of Sale (POS): Optimize merchant and checkout performance to improve conversion, approvals, and unit economics across the purchase funnel.
  • Direct to Consumer (DTC) / Card: Drive engagement, repeat usage, and lifecycle health across Affirm's app, web, and card experiences.
  • Fraud: Prevent and reduce fraud losses across the customer journey while maintaining a frictionless user experience.
  • Core Analytics: Build the quantitative research, machine learning models, performance monitoring, and scalable data foundations that enable fast, economically sound decisions.
  • Servicing: Enhance the post-origination customer experience by analyzing repayment behavior, collections strategies, and operational efficiency.
  • International Expansion: Build the measurement and decision foundations needed to sustainably launch and scale Affirm in new global markets.

About the Role

As an Analyst I in Affirm's Risk & Analytics organization, you will join one of several analytical teams working across the customer and merchant lifecycle. While the specific problems you tackle will depend on your eventual team placement, all Analyst I roles share a common foundation: using data to understand business performance, identify opportunities, and help Affirm make better decisions.

You will learn the fundamentals of consumer lending while executing scoped analytical work under the guidance of senior analysts and managers. You will leverage SQL, Python, and modern analytical tools to help optimize business strategies, monitor performance, and turn complex data into actionable insights.

  • Basic understanding of, or deep curiosity about, consumer lending regulations, fair lending principles, and how machine learning techniques apply to real-world business problems.

As the business-side EWM project lead, you take overall responsibility in our client projects for the planning, management and successful implementation of our SAP EWM initiatives from a Logistics perspective.

You ensure that our clients’ operational requirements define the framework for the solution. To achieve this, you define functional objectives together with the client, set priorities and steer internal IT, external SAP consultants and other service providers so that robust, practical and sustainable solutions are delivered.

You act as the central interface between Logistics, IT and implementation partners and represent our clients’ business interests clearly and consistently.

Your Responsibilities

  • You are responsible for the overall functional management of SAP EWM projects for our clients, including implementation, roll-out, optimization and, where applicable, migration from SAP WM to SAP EWM, from a Logistics / Supply Chain perspective.
  • Together with our clients, you define the functional objectives, requirements and success criteria for warehouse and intralogistics processes and ensure that these are implemented consistently by IT and implementation partners.
  • You coordinate and lead functional key users, process owners and, where applicable, internal EWM experts on the client side and support the development of a strong and reliable business team around EWM.
  • You manage external SAP implementation partners, developers and technical service providers from a functional perspective: you define requirements, priorities and acceptance criteria and monitor the quality of delivery.
  • You are responsible for functional test management, including test design, test cases, UAT and sign-off, as well as business-side cutover planning and the preparation and support of go-live and the hypercare phase.
  • You establish clear project governance from a business perspective, including decision-making processes, escalation paths, status reporting to Logistics management and the steering committee, as well as issue and change management.
  • You drive change communication, training and employee enablement on the client side and ensure that a capable and sustainable business organization is in place after project completion.

You combine strong logistics and process expertise with a good understanding of SAP EWM and the ability to translate business requirements into robust, practical solutions. You are comfortable navigating complex project and decision-making environments, manage different stakeholders with clarity and commitment, and challenge existing approaches with confidence. At the same time, you are comfortable working in a consulting environment and take ownership in demanding client projects.

We are a global digital transformation consulting firm with offices in Hamburg, Düsseldorf, Munich, Vienna, Atlanta, Singapore, and Shanghai.
