jobs.title: Senior Product Manager (m|w|d) Catalog Content
jobs.description:
Senior Product Manager (m|w|d) Catalog Content

Millions of people use idealo to make confident purchase decisions every day. To do that, they rely on product images, specifications, test reports, and editorial content that is accurate, helpful, and trustworthy.

In this role, you'll shape how that content comes together — from AI-generated content at scale to expert-created content where it matters most. You'll define where automation delivers good content at sound unit economics, and where human expertise is worth the investment because it genuinely changes a user's confidence in their decision.

When a category page finally has the content it needs to convert, or when an AI-generated product description performs as well as an expert-written one at a fraction of the cost, you'll see the direct impact of your work.

About your new role

  • Define the roadmap for idealo's catalog content — product images, data sheets, product and category texts, test reports, FAQs, pros & cons, and category glossaries.

  • Build and evolve the CMS and tooling that our Content and Editorial teams use to create and maintain expert content at scale.

  • Define and evolve the AI content pipeline, from generation to quality checks, in close collaboration with Data/AI Engineering.

  • Decide where expert content creates the most value for users and where AI-driven content is the right tool for good unit economics, and translate that into clear prioritization.

  • Discover, validate, and develop new content formats and features through product opportunity assessments, experimentation, and business case assessments.

  • Ensure content strategy supports SEO performance and is well-integrated into a genuinely helpful onsite experience.

  • Own the approach to translation and localization of content across idealo's international markets, balancing quality, speed, and cost.


Skills & Requirements

  • You have several years of experience as a Product Manager, ideally working on content, catalog, CMS, or data-heavy consumer products.

  • You have experience working with AI/ML-driven content generation and quality assurance at scale.

  • You have experience running product discovery, validating opportunities and making prioritization decisions based on customer value, business impact and data.

  • You have a solid understanding of SEO fundamentals and how content decisions affect organic performance.

  • You are comfortable working with experimentation and analytics tools to validate hypotheses and measure product success.

  • You take ownership and independently drive topics forward.

Senior Product Developer – Candy & Confectionery (All Genders)
jobs.description:
Senior Product Developer – Candy & Confectionery (All Genders)
YOU & AHEAD

At ahead, we are on a mission to clean up the world’s candy drawers. We make the snacks everyone actually craves: chocolate bars, protein bars, wafers, cookies, gummies and more. Our products contain up to 90% less sugar with zero compromise on taste. We are a 130-person team based in Hamburg, with our own lab, a portfolio of more than 170 SKUs and ambitious growth plans across D2C, retail, Amazon and Europe.

We are looking for a Senior Product Developer for Candy & Confectionery to own the technical development of our portfolio from the first brief through formulation, sensory validation, scale-up and launch.

As our Senior Product Developer, you will bring technical depth to one of our most important categories and make sure every decision works in the real world: in the recipe, in the factory and in the customer’s hands.

Are you a food developer who knows how to turn a great idea into a product people genuinely love? Someone who can balance taste, texture, stability, cost, compliance and timing while getting the product over the line? If you like taking ownership and enjoy solving real product problems, we would love to hear from you! 


YOUR TASKS

  • End-to-End Product Development: You own candy and confectionery projects from brief to launch. You translate requirements into clear technical targets, develop and optimise formulations, oversee trials, sensory validation and technical decisions.

  • Sugar Reduction & Product Performance: You develop reduced-sugar and no-added-sugar products without compromising on taste. You understand how ingredients affect texture, processing, stability and shelf life, and make clear trade-offs between quality, cost, compliance and speed.

  • Sensory, Shelf Life & Scale-Up: You plan and coordinate sensory, shelf-life and stability testing. You prepare for pilot and industrial trials, work closely with co-manufacturers, troubleshoot issues and follow solutions through to production.

  • Specifications, Suppliers & Compliance: You manage formulations, specifications, technical documentation, ingredients and samples. Together with our Quality team, you ensure that food law, labelling, allergen, nutritional and claims requirements are considered from the start.

  • Cross-Functional Ownership: You work closely with Product, Quality, Operations, Procurement, Brand, Retail and Marketing. You communicate clearly, flag risks early, challenge assumptions and keep projects moving.

  • Building Better NPD Processes: You document decisions and learnings, create clear handovers and help make product development more structured and predictable as ahead grows.


YOUR PROFILE

  • You bring 5+ years of experience in food product development, R&D, or NPD, with a track record from brief through formulation, sensory validation, scale-up, and launch. Hands-on experience in gummies, candy, chocolate, confectionery, or a related sweet-goods category is mandatory.

  • You understand how taste, texture, processing, stability, shelf life, ingredients and production realities come together in a successful product. You have experience with sugar-reduction or no-added-sugar systems and know how to balance product performance with consumer expectations.

  • You have worked with ingredient suppliers and co-manufacturers and have been involved in pilot or industrial-scale production. You are comfortable with specifications, technical documentation, and food-law requirements.

  • You take ownership and follow through. You are structured without being bureaucratic, comfortable with ambiguity and willing to challenge a brief, assumption or timeline when needed. You communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders and enjoy working as a senior individual contributor without direct reports initially.

  • You hold a degree or equivalent training in food science, food technology, chemistry, nutrition science, ecotrophology, or a comparable field. You communicate confidently in German and English.


WHAT MAKES YOUR PROFILE COMPLETE

  • Experience launching 10+ food products, ideally across multiple markets.

  • Experience working with gummies, candy, chocolate bars, cookies, filled confectionery or similar products.

  • Strong knowledge of sugar reduction, sweetener systems, fibres and texture management.

  • Experience planning, conducting or interpreting sensory tests, shelf-life studies and stability testing.

  • Background in better-for-you food, functional food, private-label NPD, or a fast-growing consumer brand.

  • Experience delivering products into D2C and retail channels across DACH or Europe.


AND WHY AHEAD?

Working at ahead is more than just a job - it’s your opportunity to develop as a professional and as a person, while shaping the future of snacking. Our mission is to make low sugar the new standard, and we pour that ambition into every product we create. You’ll become part of a team where international talent, startup drive, real impact, and true ownership come together.

  • Hypergrowth Environment: If you're looking for greenfield, creative freedom, and real impact, you're in the right place. We're a team that is scaling fast - with purpose
  • Great Workspace: A central office in the heart of Hamburg near the Alster, top equipment (MacBook), snacks, drinks, plenty of ahead products - and yes, a ping-pong table. We’re also pet-friendly, so you can always bring your furry friend along
  • Amazing Team: Young, international, ambitious - inspiring colleagues who collaborate, support each other, and genuinely enjoy working together
  • Career Growth: Develop through cross-functional projects, structured feedback cycles, and a steep learning curve in a dynamic, high growth environment. We offer a fair, attractive salary with role-dependent bonus opportunities
  • Great Benefits: Fuel yourself with ahead snacks, drinks, and merch - we’ve got you covered. On top: a €50 monthly allowance to spend as you like - Urban Sports Club, mobility options, or vouchers from your favorite brands (IKEA, Rewe, Rossmann and more)
  • Vacation Days: Enjoy 28 vacation days plus two extra days off on December 24 (Christmas Eve) and December 31 (New Year’s Eve)
  • Events & Offsites: Regular after-work hangouts and legendary annual team offsites you won’t forget
This role is based in Hamburg, with the flexibility of up to 2 home office days per week and the option to work from abroad for agreed upon periods. If this resonates with you, we're excited to go ahead with you!

jobs.title: Senior Process Engieer
jobs.description:
Senior Process Engieer
ABOUT US

tozero is Europe’s leading deep-tech startup specializing in the recycling of
lithium-ion batteries. Committed to accelerating decarbonization and transforming
the material life cycle, we’re actively crafting sustainable recycling solutions for a
cleaner and more innovative future.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a Senior Process Engineer to take a leading technical role in the
design, scale-up, commissioning and ramp up of our battery recycling processes.
This role sits at the intersection of technology development, process engineering,
and industrial scale-up. You will translate experimental and operational data into
robust process designs, challenge engineering assumptions, and ensure that our
future plants are built on solid fundamentals.
Your focus will be on the processes that matter most to our technology — graphite
and lithium extraction. By working closely with R&D, Operations and external
engineering partners, you will actively lead and engage in activities associated with:
a) engineering design; b) commissioning and ramp up; c) process development.
We are looking for someone who is comfortable working in a production
environment, but who can also take a step back and understand what the data is
telling us, and engineer the process we need at different scales.


WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT

Must Have's:
1. Future Plant Design & Scale-up
● Own key process design activities for our next-generation plants.
● Develop and review PFDs, P&IDs, mass and energy balances, process
descriptions and equipment specifications for future capacity expansions.

● Translate pilot and industrial operating data into reliable engineering design
criteria and scale-up assumptions.
● Perform process calculations and equipment sizing to ensure our future
plants are designed based on validated engineering data rather than
theoretical assumptions alone.
2. Targeted Process Expertise & Optimization
● Become a technical reference for some of our most critical process steps.
● Apply strong chemical engineering fundamentals to the optimization of
graphite and lithium extraction and post-processing.
● Identify the parameters controlling yield, purity and process stability and
translate these insights into concrete process improvements.
● Work closely with R&D and Operations while maintaining a strong focus on
process performance and technology development rather than daily
troubleshooting.
3. Data Analysis & Process Modeling
● Turn plant data into engineering decisions.
● Evaluate operational and experimental data, build and validate mass balances
and process models, and identify gaps between expected and actual process
performance.
● Define what data needs to be collected to support future scale-up decisions.
● Technically guide data analysts and other engineering functions to ensure
that models and analytics remain grounded in physical and chemical reality.
● Translate analysis into clear recommendations for process upgrades and
future plant designs.
4. Commissioning & Process Validation
● Make sure what we designed actually works.
● Participate in FATs/SATs, commissioning activities and process performance
validation for new equipment and plant expansions.
● Develop acceptance and process validation criteria based on the original
design intent.
● Evaluate commissioning and operational data to confirm that installed
systems achieve their calculated performance targets.
● Work closely with Operations during handover while ensuring clear ownership
transfers once the process meets its design criteria.
5. Operational Readiness, Process Safety & SOPs
● Design processes that can be operated safely and consistently.
● Translate process design and engineering intent into clear Standard Operating
Procedures (SOPs), operating envelopes and process documentation.
● Participate actively in HAZOPs, LOPAs, and other process safety reviews,
ensuring that process risks are identified and addressed during design rather
than after installation.
● Support Operations in understanding the design basis and critical process
parameters of newly commissioned systems.

Nice-to-have's:
Vendor & EPC Coordination
● Represent tozero's process requirements with external engineering partners
and equipment suppliers.
● Prepare and review technical specifications, vendor proposals and engineering
documentation.
● Challenge unsupported assumptions, identify over-engineered solutions and
ensure equipment is correctly sized for our process.
● Support technical bid evaluations and equipment selection, balancing process
performance, CAPEX, operability and scalability.
● Act as a strong technical counterpart to EPCs, engineering contractors and
equipment vendors throughout project execution.


Your profile

You have a strong chemical/process engineering foundation and enjoy solving
technically complex problems with a combination of first-principles engineering and
real plant data.
● Degree in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Metallurgical
Engineering or a related technical field.
● Ideally 5+ years of experience in process engineering within the chemical,
hydrometallurgy, battery, mining, minerals, recycling or related process
industries; specific expertise in graphite and lithium extraction and
post-processing is highly preferred.
● Strong experience with process design and scale-up, including PFDs, P&IDs,
mass/energy balances and equipment sizing.
● Comfortable working with industrial datasets and translating operational data
into engineering models and decisions.
● Experience with solid-liquid separation, precipitation, flotation,
hydrometallurgy or mineral processing is highly valuable.
● Able to critically review vendor proposals and confidently challenge technical
assumptions.
● Strong experience supporting commissioning and process validation of
industrial equipment or plants.
● Familiarity with process safety methodologies such as HAZOP and LOPA.
● Comfortable moving between detailed calculations, engineering
documentation and the actual plant.
● Strong communicator who can work effectively across R&D, Engineering,
Operations, suppliers and EPC partners.
● Fluent English; German is a plus.


Why us?

Our technology is moving from first-of-a-kind industrial operations toward
increasingly larger and more standardized plants.
The Senior Process Engineer will help us make that transition successfully: turning
what we learn from today's plant into the engineering basis for tomorrow's plants
while supporting commissioning and ramping up efforts.
You will directly influence process performance, equipment selection, CAPEX and the
technical architecture of our future facilities — helping ensure that every new scale is
safer, simpler, more efficient and better engineered than the one before it.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
Senior Product Manager

Menlo Security is the leader in Browser Security for human and agentic workforces. Our mission is to enable humans and agents to connect, communicate, and collaborate securely, without compromise. The Menlo Browser Security Platform protects organizations from cyberattacks by stopping threats across the web, documents, and email before they reach the user. With Menlo Agent Runtime Security (MARS), that protection now extends to the AI agents working alongside every employee. Menlo Security is trusted by major global businesses, including Fortune 500 companies and government agencies, to protect their most valuable asset, their data, and is backed by top-tier investors.

About the Role

Summary

Menlo Security is building MARS for Agents (Menlo Agent Runtime Security), our product line for securing autonomous and hybrid AI agents. This is a category still being defined — standards, architecture patterns, and competitive positioning are all forming in real time, with competitors ranging from established network security vendors to a wave of new agent-security startups.

 

We are hiring an experienced Product Manager / Product Owner to take end-to-end ownership of a significant, technically complex area within MARS for Agents. The specific scope will be defined in partnership with the hiring manager based on team needs and the background of the person in this role, and will span identity and security concepts, relevant technical protocols, and platform integration and partnership work. The role operates with a high degree of autonomy day to day, working from strategic direction set by the Head of Product, in an environment that runs agile development at high velocity while actively building the process and rigor needed to scale a growing product line.

 

This is also a team that works the way it builds: AI assistants and LLM-based tools are part of the daily toolkit here — used to synthesize customer and competitive signal, pressure-test requirements, and prototype against MCP clients and agent runtimes before a single line of production code is written. The person in this role will be defining security for a category they are already a fluent, curious user of.

Outcomes & KPIs

Key Outcome(s) Owned:

  • End-to-end ownership of an assigned surface area of MARS for Agents — across capabilities such as the agent registry, Claude integration, Microsoft Copilot integration, MCP Server, MCP Proxy, and LLM proxy — from researched opportunity, to written requirement, to shipped and supported capability.

  • A current, honest, decision-changing competitive point of view for the agent-security category that the wider go-to-market organization can rely on.

Success Metrics / KPIs

  • Roadmap delivery: committed roadmap items for the owned surfaces shipped within the target release window.

  • Requirements quality: Reduction in mid-sprint requirement clarifications and rework attributable to ambiguous PRDs or acceptance criteria, measured via engineering feedback each quarter.

  • Enablement coverage: 100% of shipped capabilities in the owned area have current capability documentation and a delivered briefing to support and solutions engineering at or before release.

  • Adoption of shipped capability: Customer adoption or usage of newly released capabilities against a target set at launch, tracked for 90 days post-release.

  • Competitive influence: At least one documented roadmap or positioning decision per quarter, traceable to a published competitive finding.

What You'll Do

  • Own inbound product direction for your area. Research emerging agentic AI capabilities, attacker techniques, and adjacent standards (MCP, A2A, OWASP agentic-security guidance, agent identity frameworks) to determine what MARS for Agents should build next across the agent registry, Claude integration, Microsoft Copilot integration, MCP Server, MCP Proxy, and LLM proxy.

  • Turn signal into engineering-ready requirements. Translate market, customer, and competitive input into clear PRDs, user stories, and acceptance criteria — using LLM-based tools to synthesize call notes, support tickets, standards documents, and usage data into prioritization insight, while retaining full accountability for the judgment calls and the accuracy of what you write.

  • Own and groom the backlog. Make day-to-day prioritization calls across your surfaces within the strategic guardrails set by the Head of Product, and partner directly with engineering through the full build cycle: refinement, in-sprint questions, review, and release.

  • Validate before you specify. Use AI coding assistants, MCP clients, and agent runtimes hands-on to prototype and stress-test proposed behavior — so requirements are grounded in how agents actually behave, not just how they are documented to behave. Define success metrics for what you ship and track them post-release.

  • Enable the field. Brief technical support and solutions engineering on new and existing capabilities, and maintain current capability documentation for your area that clearly separates documented and shipping facts from planned work and open questions, so the field never over-promises. Be the trusted authority on what your part of MARS does today, what is coming, and what it deliberately does not do yet.

  • Engage customers, sales, and marketing. Join customer and prospect conversations periodically to gather requirements, pressure-test positioning, and support technical evaluations; support the sales team with technical Q&A, competitive objection-handling, and input on proposals and decks; and work with product marketing on messaging, positioning, and launch content.

  • Run competitive analysis that changes decisions. Continuously track competitors relevant to MARS for Agents — network/SSE-SASE incumbents (Palo Alto Networks, Zscaler, Cloudflare, Netskope), agent-identity and IAM players (Okta, CyberArk), MCP gateway vendors, and emerging agent-security pure-plays — and maintain a clear point of view on where MARS leads, where it currently trails, and what capabilities are commoditizing. Feed those findings directly into requirements, positioning, and roadmap prioritization.

Functional Competencies

Required:

  • 6–10+ years of product management or product owner experience, ideally in B2B SaaS, enterprise infrastructure, or security software, including a track record of owning a complex, technical product area end to end.

  • Demonstrated ability to write clear, engineering-ready requirements (PRDs, user stories, acceptance criteria) and to own a backlog end to end for a technically complex product surface.

  • Comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy. This role receives strategic direction rather than daily instruction, and the person in it should be able to take a goal and drive it through research, requirements, engineering partnership, and launch across multiple related surfaces at once — with the support of a collaborative product and engineering team.

  • Comfort operating at high velocity. Our engineering organization runs agile at a fast cadence, and this role also helps bring the process and rigor needed to make the product scalable, so both muscles matter.

  • Solid working knowledge of AI agent technology: how LLMs and AI agents operate, the difference between autonomous and human-in-the-loop (hybrid) agents, tool and function calling, and — specifically — the MCP (Model Context Protocol) ecosystem (servers, clients, tool calls) at a depth sufficient to write requirements for an MCP Server and an MCP Proxy, not just discuss them conceptually.

  • Real cybersecurity background, with working familiarity in areas such as identity and access management, proxy and gateway architectures (forward proxy, reverse proxy, secure web gateway / SSE / SASE), and content or traffic inspection. Deep specialization in every area is not required, but enough fluency to engage credibly with engineering and with technical customers is.

  • Hands-on, regular personal use of AI tools — for example Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code / Cowork, GitHub Copilot, or similar — including some exposure to how they use MCP or other tool-calling integrations.

jobs.title: Brand Design Lead
jobs.description:
Brand Design Lead

Nash powers the logistics infrastructure behind some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, and 7-Eleven, along with platforms like Shopify and Toast. As we scale, our brand needs to scale with us. We're hiring our first dedicated Brand Designer to craft, shape, and build the visual identity of the platform that is becoming foundational to modern commerce.

The Role

We are right in the middle of defining and rolling out a new Nash brand. Strategy, visual language, motion system, photography direction, the wordmark, the website, the pitch, the booth, the apparel: all of it is being built right now. This is a rare moment to author a brand from close to zero and watch it become the visual identity of a category.

You'll report directly to our Chief Growth Officer (who spent their career building and leading marketing, growth, and product organizations at companies like Twilio, Plaid, and Salesforce). You'll work alongside our CEO, our CTO, and a small, senior, fast-moving cross-functional group across product, engineering, and growth. The bar for taste, craft, and strategic thinking on this team is high, and the trajectory for someone strong in this seat is significant.

How We Work: A.I.-Native, By Default

Brand design at Nash is A.I.-native. We are looking for a designer who has fundamentally rewired how they work around A.I., not a designer who occasionally uses ChatGPT for copy or the occasional inspo image. A designer who reaches for Claude, Cursor, Figma Make, Midjourney, and Runway as instinctively as they reach for the pen tool. Whose entire workflow is built around using A.I. to get to better outcomes faster.

The reason is straightforward: the speed and surface area of what one designer can ship has changed by an order of magnitude in the last eighteen months. We want someone who feels that in their bones and uses it to compound their craft, not replace it.

Don't get us wrong...we deeply value the soul, the personality, the whimsy...the magic that can only come from a real designer. This is not an A.I. slop-house! But we need to pair the magic of the human touch with the pace and velocity that A.I. tools bring.

In practice, this looks like going from a verbal idea to a working interactive prototype the same afternoon, generating ten directions for a campaign before lunch and using your own taste to pick the one worth refining, prototyping a marketing site section in code with Claude or Cursor and handing a working artifact to engineering instead of a static comp, and treating prompt craft, model choice, and tool-chaining as part of your design practice.

If your reaction to a new A.I. tool is curiosity and a Saturday afternoon experiment, you'll fit here. If you believe that A.I. will never replace ... then you probably won't.

What You'll Do

- Translate, Define and Evolve the new Nash brand strategy into a complete, living visual system: identity applications, motion principles, photography direction, illustration style, typography in use

- Design and build the marketing site in Figma and Webflow; own landing pages, campaign pages, product launch moments, and the visual story we tell at events like NRF, Manifest, and Shoptalk

- Bring the Nash visual language to life through motion: site interactions, product reveals, social, keynote, and trade show

- Own the visual layer of the demand engine: pitch decks, one-pagers, customer-facing PDFs, partner materials, the work that helps close deals

- Prototype quickly using A.I. tools (Claude, Cursor, Figma Make, Runway, Midjourney) to compress the loop from idea to artifact

- Ensure the final touch of any design is always human, authentic, and has soul. While we use A.I. to prototype, we care about that hard to define sparkle that comes from something hand crafted.

- Build installations and real-world experiences that are fascinatingly real - in a world full of A.I. slop, our brand leans into very tangible, real world things.

- Set the bar for craft across the company; teach the rest of the team how to use A.I. tools to get there faster without losing taste

- Partner with engineering to ship expressions of the brand surfaces in product too

- Contribute to the brand system itself: patterns, components, prompts, and rituals that scale how Nash shows up everywhere

Requirements

- 6+ years experience in brand or product design, with shipped work that demonstrates strong craft across identity, web, motion, and campaign

- Has owned a brand or a major brand evolution at a high-growth technology company, and can talk about the decisions and tradeoffs behind it

- Active, daily use of LLMs (we use Claude Code / Claude Cowork and A.I. prototyping tools (e.g. Replit) as a core part of your design workflow

- Fluent in Figma and Webflow; comfortable in After Effects and Illustrator; curious about whatever ships next

- Systems thinker who can hold the whole brand in their head while obsessing over the kerning of a single headline

- Strong opinions, communicated clearly, updated quickly when the evidence changes

- Comfortable working alongside engineers and operators on things that have to actually function in the real world

- Bonus: built a marketing site end to end in Webflow at production scale; shipped motion work that lived on a homepage or a keynote; prior experience designing for B2B platforms, infrastructure, or logistics; released your own side project using A.I. prototyping tools

How to Apply

Send us your portfolio, a short note on the brand work you're proudest of and why, and one example of how A.I. has changed the way you design. If you'd rather skip the cover letter and send a Replit prototype, a Loom, or a Figma file, that is very much encouraged.

More about Nash

Nash is the platform that powers modern logistics.

Commerce has inverted. For decades, customers came to where products and services were. Now products and services come to them, on their terms, in real time. That shift has turned every company into a logistics company, even though almost none of them were built to be one. Couriers, fleets, gig workers, parcel carriers, in-store labor, and increasingly autonomous systems all have to be coordinated in real time, against tighter windows and rising expectations, with hard-fought customer trust on the line.

Nash unifies decisioning, execution, and capacity into a single programmable platform. Real-time, AI-native intelligence determines what should happen, operational control executes it, and the platform dynamically orchestrates capacity from any source: a company's own fleets, partners, or the Nash delivery network. Whether a job involves a courier, a gig driver, an internal fleet, a store employee, a technician, or an autonomous vehicle, Nash selects the right resource and manages execution through completion.

We power delivery and logistics for some of the most recognizable brands in commerce, including Walmart, Urban Outfitters, 7-Eleven, and Woolworths, alongside platforms like Shopify and Toast. Over the next decade, logistics will become as foundational to commerce as payments, cloud, and connectivity. Nash is the platform that powers it.

Nash was founded in 2021 by Mahmoud Ghulman (2x Founder, MIT) and Aziz Alghunaim (2x Founder, 2x YC, Ex-Palantir, MIT) and is backed by Y Combinator, a16z, and other top investors. We are headquartered in San Francisco.

What You’ll Love About Us

✅ Early-stage, well-funded startup – directly impact the company and grow your career!
✅ Quarterly broader team on-sites to bond with teammates
✅ Competitive compensation and opportunity for equity
✅ Flexible paid time off
✅ Health, dental, and vision insurance

jobs.title: Product Manager, Courier Delivery Experience
jobs.description:
Product Manager, Courier Delivery Experience

About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

We seek a Product Manager to join our Courier and Delivery Experience (CDX) team. This role will focus on ensuring world-class courier and consumer delivery experiences while continually evolving the delivery process with a future-oriented mindset. The Courier and Delivery Experience team owns the experiences that elevate every Wolt delivery, from the moment a courier opens the app to every order they accept, all the way to dropping an order off at the customer's doorstep. The team sits at the intersection of a multi-sided marketplace product, real-world operations, and safety, and the work directly moves how reliable Wolt feels to consumers and how satisfied our couriers are when delivering.

You will play a crucial role in shaping the courier experience, ensuring that our couriers feel valued and supported while enhancing the efficiency of deliveries. By blending operational expertise with a deep understanding of courier needs, you will improve the user journey from onboarding couriers to completing deliveries. From designing new features that boost courier satisfaction to refining delivery processes, your work will contribute to key metrics across courier engagement, performance, and satisfaction. You will also be influential in shaping the evolution of the live delivery experience for our courier partners, the merchant courier interaction at pickup and the consumer courier interaction at the doorstep via the Courier app surfaces. 

The ideal candidate will have an exceptional track record in product management, with proven success in working with cross-functional teams across engineering, design, product, and operations. You will define the vision and roadmap for courier and delivery experiences across multiple projects. Working in partnership with business stakeholders, you will also collaborate on cross-team initiatives, contributing to the broader business strategy while ensuring a deep understanding of the courier experience.

Join us in shaping the future of delivery, where every delivery is an opportunity for delight and loyalty.

Our humble expectations

You could come to this role from various backgrounds, but ideally, you bring:

  • Several years of experience in product management, specializing in consumer-facing products
  • Expertise in developing user-centric products, with the ability to address complex user experience-related challenges.
  • Demonstrated expertise in supporting cross-functional teams and fostering operational excellence in fast-paced, high-demand industries.
  • Proven track record in building products influencing cross-functional teams, including engineering, data, design, and operations.
  • High ownership and collaborative capabilities, making thoughtful decisions, and focusing on product details to ensure execution aligns with the vision.
  • Strong ability to define, execute, and measure meaningful OKRs, ensuring alignment with company-wide goals and fostering bottom-up alignment from your team.
  • Ability to focus on the bigger picture, creating solutions that benefit couriers, operations, and customer experiences across the organization.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, able to work effectively with diverse internal teams and external partners, while confidently engaging with leadership in a high-visibility role

The position will be filled as soon as we find the right person, so make sure to apply as soon as you realize you really, really want to join us!

The compensation will be a negotiable combination of monthly pay and DoorDash RSUs. The latter makes it exceptionally easy to be excited about our company growing and doing well, as you'll own a piece of the pie.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Beware of recruitment scams: DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about our legitimate recruiting process at Recruitment Scam Awareness - DoorDash .

jobs.title: Engineering Manager (m/w/d) – Core Team
jobs.description:
Engineering Manager (m/w/d) – Core Team
Deine Aufgaben

Wir bauen die Software, mit der Mieterstromprojekte laufen: Zählerdaten rein, Abrechnung raus, und alles dazwischen. Das Core Team verantwortet das Betreiberportal, das Produkt, auf dem der laufende Betrieb unserer Kunden steht. Es ist unser fachlich tiefstes Team, und es wächst.

Das Betreiberportal ist kein generisches SaaS. Es bildet die Energiewirtschaft ab: Messstellenbetrieb, Marktkommunikation, Netzentgelte, Umlagen, Abrechnung nach Regeln, die der Gesetzgeber schreibt und regelmäßig ändert. Wer hier priorisiert, muss verstehen, was eine Anforderung für den Betreiber wirtschaftlich bedeutet und was passiert, wenn sie falsch umgesetzt wird.

Dafür suchen wir eine Person, die das Team führt und das Geschäft dahinter versteht. Nicht als Durchreiche für Tickets und nicht als Architekt, der alles selbst entscheidet, sondern als jemand, der Business-Anforderungen in technische Entscheidungen übersetzt und dafür sorgt, dass gute Entwickler gute Arbeit machen können: klare Ziele, wenig Reibung, ehrliches Feedback, verlässliche Lieferung.

Der Weg dahin ist bewusst gewählt: Du startest für rund sechs Monate als Entwickler im Core Team. Du baust Features, machst Reviews und lernst Codebasis, Fachlichkeit und Menschen von innen kennen. Danach übernimmst du die Führung des Teams. Wer ein Team führen will, das er nie von innen gesehen hat, führt es an dem vorbei, was zählt.

Technisch: Python mit Django und Django Ninja im Backend, React mit TypeScript im Frontend, PostgreSQL mit TimescaleDB, deployt auf Kubernetes per GitOps mit ArgoCD. KI-Coding-Assistenten sind fester Teil des Workflows. In den ersten Monaten schreibst du diesen Code selbst. Danach musst du ihn weiter lesen können und verstehen, worüber dein Team diskutiert.

In den ersten sechs Monaten

  • Du arbeitest als Entwickler im Core Team: Features end-to-end, Reviews, Deployments, Support-Fälle. Ohne Sonderrolle

  • Du lernst die Fachlichkeit von Messkonzept bis Abrechnung und die Geschichte der Codebasis, inklusive der Stellen, an denen sie weh tut

  • Du baust Vertrauen zu den Menschen im Team auf, weil du mit ihnen arbeitest und nicht über ihnen

Danach

  • Du führst das Core Team: Einstellung, Onboarding, 1:1s, Entwicklung, Feedback. Die Menschen im Team sind deine erste Verantwortung

  • Du verantwortest die Lieferung: Zusammen mit Product priorisierst du nach wirtschaftlichem Wert und regulatorischem Druck, planst realistisch und sorgst dafür, dass Zugesagtes fertig wird

  • Du bringst Fachverständnis in die Produktentscheidungen ein: Du erkennst, wann eine Anforderung aus dem Markt kommt, wann aus einem einzelnen Kunden, und wann aus einem Missverständnis

  • Du hältst die technische Qualität hoch, ohne selbst der Flaschenhals zu sein: Du moderierst Architekturentscheidungen, forderst Tests und Reviews ein und schaffst Raum für Refactoring

  • Du bist die Schnittstelle zu Product, Support und den anderen Engineering-Teams, und du löst Konflikte, bevor sie im Sprint landen

  • Du machst Probleme sichtbar: Wenn etwas nicht klappt, sagst du es früh und mit Vorschlag statt spät und mit Ausrede

  • Du gestaltest Prozesse so, dass sie dem Team dienen, und schaffst die ab, die es nicht tun


Dein Profil

  • Mehrere Jahre Erfahrung als Softwareentwickler mit Web-Anwendungen in Produktion. Du kannst in Django und React produktiv arbeiten oder dich in wenigen Wochen dort einfinden

  • Erfahrung in der Führung eines Entwicklungsteams, als Engineering Manager, Team Lead oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle mit Personalverantwortung

  • Du kannst ein Datenmodell beurteilen und eine Architekturdiskussion moderieren, ohne sie an dich zu reißen

  • Du willst wieder oder weiter Code schreiben, bevor du führst, und siehst das als Vorteil, nicht als Umweg

  • Erfahrung in der Energiewirtschaft, idealerweise in Messstellenbetrieb, Abrechnung, Marktkommunikation oder Mieterstrom. Du kennst Begriffe wie Messkonzept, MaLo oder OBIS nicht nur aus Wikipedia

  • Business-Verständnis: Du denkst vom Geschäftsmodell des Betreibers her, nicht vom Feature. Du kannst erklären, welche Anforderung Umsatz sichert, welche Risiko reduziert und welche nur schön ist

  • Du gibst direktes Feedback und hältst es aus, direktes Feedback zu bekommen

  • Du kannst Nein sagen, zu Stakeholdern und zum eigenen Team, und begründen, warum

  • Du fühlst dich in einem Startup wohl, in dem Strukturen noch entstehen und du sie mitgestaltest

  • Deutsch mindestens auf C1-Niveau, weil Fachlichkeit, Kunden und ein Großteil der Kommunikation deutsch sind


Warum wir?

  • Eine Führungsrolle mit echtem Gestaltungsspielraum in einer wachsenden Engineering-Organisation, mit einem Einstieg, der dich nicht ins kalte Wasser wirft

  • Direkter Draht zum CTO und Mitsprache bei der Teamstruktur, nicht nur bei der Umsetzung

  • Hybrid in Hamburg: 1-2 Tage im Office, der Rest remote

  • Ein Team ohne Hierarchieebenen. Wer eine bessere Idee hat, setzt sie um

  • Zuschuss zu Deutschlandticket, Bikeleasing, Urban Sports Club und betrieblicher Altersvorsorge

  • Ein Produkt, das die Energiewende konkret voranbringt, statt sie nur in die Präsentation zu schreiben

Metaview is an applied AI lab building AI coworkers for some of the world's most ambitious recruiting teams. Hear directly from our customers. The challenge is not another chatbot. It is software that can pursue a hiring objective, operate within real workflows, seek judgment at the right moment, and earn a customer's trust.

We have one value: velocity.

Not motion for its own sake, but real progress. We ship every day, ship on Fridays, and skip the tickets, roadmaps, and design-doc theater. Every builder on the team orchestrates a stack of agents, and we ship 8x what we did a year ago with the same small team. That pace needs a designer whose thinking keeps up: someone who can go from a vague problem to a clear, high-fidelity answer in hours, not sprints, and put it in front of engineers and customers while the idea is still hot. Process stays light, standards stay high, and feedback loops stay short.

What you'll design

Day to day, you'll own:

  • the look and feel of new product experiences across the hiring workflow, from first sketch to final pixels

  • interfaces that make AI agents feel transparent, trustworthy, and like a real coworker

  • the moments where conversational signal becomes something a user can see, trust, and act on

  • fast, high-fidelity prototypes that prove or kill an idea before anyone commits to building it

  • the craft bar for the whole product: motion, density, hierarchy, and the details that make it feel inevitable

What you'll own

In your first 3–6 months, you should:

  • own meaningful product areas end-to-end, from problem definition through rollout, in close partnership with engineering

  • set how Metaview's AI products look, feel, and behave in real customer workflows

  • turn messy, ambiguous problems into interfaces that feel obvious in hindsight

What we're after

We're likely to be excited by people who:

  • have designed and shipped beautiful, complex products in fast-moving software environments

  • have a real point of view on products: what's great, what's broken, and what they'd change

What you bring

Helpful signals include experience with:

Street Group is one of the fastest-growing PropTech companies in the UK. We want to be the leading creator of delightful experiences for everybody involved in buying, selling, renting and letting property, regardless of their involvement, to improve the industry for everybody by elevating UK Estate Agencies through world-class technology.

We're now looking for a Lead Product Designer - the most senior individual contributor for design within a product domain. This is predominantly an IC role: you'll set the design bar for an entire domain through the quality of your own work, the patterns you contribute, and the way you raise the designers around you. We're flexible on this for the right person, if you've got management experience, or want to line-manage one or two designers alongside the IC work, let's talk.

We want someone who is tired of the "feature factory" grind, who is past needing to be told what's worth working on, and who is ready to set the design direction for a domain in one of the most exciting PropTech companies in the UK.

If you look at most UX job ads, you see a laundry list of requirements. We prefer to tell you how we actually operate so you can decide if this is the right environment for you.

  • At Street Group, design is a strategic seat. Lead Product Designers drive roadmap conversations alongside their product and engineering counterparts, not respond to them.

  • Our users rely on us to run their businesses, so they love talking to us. You can spin up a call and validate a prototype instantly. We don't guess; we ask.

  • We move at pace, including on strategic work. Strategy isn't a separate, slower track here - we test it by shipping.

Here's what you can expect to be working on as an L6 Lead Product Designer at Street Group

  • Own the design vision and execution for a product domain. Translate strategic direction into the most ambiguous, cross-cutting, or strategically important pieces of design work.

  • Set the craft bar through your own output. The work you ship is the reference point for what good looks like in your area.

  • Own the cross-cutting design problems: patterns across multiple features, flows across multiple surfaces, the coherence of the domain's experience as a whole.

  • Mentor and raise the bar of the designers around you - through critique, pairing, and modelling what excellent design looks like.

  • Drive AI thinking strategically - both in your own workflow (Claude Code, in-product changes, prototype testing) and in what we ship to users. You'll have a strong view on what makes a good AI feature in this domain vs a gimmicky one.

Why you should (and shouldn't) apply

You should apply if:

  • You've operated at senior IC level in a modern product org and you want broader scope to influence what gets built.

  • You're commercially fluent. You've made design trade-offs informed by how the product makes money, not just by user preference. You can name those trade-offs and defend them either way.

  • You define what success looks like before you ship, and you read the result against it after. Metrics, support data, customer feedback - you go and look.

  • You have strong, well-formed views on AI in product design and have put them into practice. You can articulate when AI is the right design solution and when it isn't.

  • You move at pace on strategic work, not just on features.

You probably shouldn't apply if:

  • You're looking for the next pay band up from Senior with broadly similar expectations. This is not a "Senior+" role. Lead expects materially more scope, autonomy, judgment, and ownership of outcomes.

  • You've never shipped design work where you defined a success measure upfront and checked the result afterwards. We need someone who already operates that way.

  • You've never had to make a commercial trade-off - design that's user-optimal but expensive to build, or design that doesn't move retention.

  • You'd struggle to explain how AI is changing what you ship, not just how you work. AI fluency is non-negotiable at this level.

  • You expect to be handed a brief. At L6 you identify what's worth doing and bring the case for it.

A bit about you

  • Experience: Roughly 8+ years of Product/UX Design experience, with a track record at senior IC level. SaaS or complex product experience is strongly preferred.

  • Outcomes, not artefacts: You can point to design work you've shipped where you wrote the success measure upfront and read the result after release. You know what worked, what didn't, and what you'd do differently.

  • Commercial fluency: You understand how the products you've worked on make money and you've made trade-offs informed by that.

  • AI: Comfortable using AI across your workflow and equally comfortable thinking strategically about AI in the products you design - what makes a good AI feature, what the failure modes are, what to build now vs later.

  • Craft: Your work is exemplary and you can articulate it clearly enough to teach. You have views on interaction quality, hierarchy, motion, microcopy - and you can defend them.

  • Cross-functional: Comfortable as a peer at the table with product and engineering counterparts in your domain. Drive direction; don't wait for it.

  • Open to flex: This is predominantly an IC role, but we're not rigid about it. If you've line-managed before, or want to take on one or two direct reports alongside the IC work, we're open to that conversation.

Research has shown that women tend to rule themselves out of applying for jobs unless they meet 100% of the requirements. If you fall into that category and are about to rule yourself out based on the above criteria, please consider applying anyway. We'd love to see your application.

Velocity Account Executive - DACH Market

About Prelude

Prelude is redefining how companies authenticate and onboard users - turning what's traditionally a cost center into a growth lever.

Our flagship product lets businesses send OTP codes with the best price-to-conversion ratio on the market, dynamically selecting the most effective channel in real time (optimized SMS, WhatsApp, and more) while actively blocking spam and fraud that legacy providers miss.

Founded in 2022 by former Zenly team members who lived the pain of broken SMS authentication firsthand, we're already serving fast-growing companies across Europe and are expanding into the US.

But authentication is only the starting point - we're building the platform for trust at scale, with an ambitious roadmap of market-defining products ahead.

Why join us

Today, we're a team of 60 and growing, based in Paris, building products that power secure and high-performance user onboarding for companies across the world. We believe small, highly skilled teams outperform large, fragmented organizations, and we are intentional about staying focused on impact, quality, and speed.

We operate with a flat org structure and value in-person collaboration, which helps ideas move faster, decisions stay grounded, and teams take full ownership of what they build.
Our values

  • Care
    We care deeply about our customers, our teammates, and the quality and reliability of what we ship.

  • Bias for Action
    We move fast, test in the real world, and iterate quickly rather than over-optimizing in theory.

  • Ownership
    We take responsibility end to end, from identifying problems to delivering outcomes and learning from results.

This Account Executive role at Prelude is built for a high-energy, outbound-first seller who thrives prospecting and knows how to move fast. You'll be hunting and closing SMB deals at volume - owning the full cycle through to signed contract. If you love the grind of building pipeline from scratch, have a knack for quick discovery, and get a buzz from a fast close, this is the role for you.

What will you be doing?

  • Running a high-volume outbound motion - cold calling, cold emailing, and LinkedIn prospecting daily to build pipeline from the ground up, as well as working closely with our high performing BDRs

  • Owning the full sales cycle end-to-end, through to closed-won, typically within a short sales cycle

  • Quickly qualifying SMB prospects through sharp, conversational discovery to identify pain and move deals forward fast

  • Delivering concise, punchy demos tailored to SMB buyers

  • Hitting and exceeding monthly and quarterly targets for pipeline generation, activities, and closed revenue

  • Keeping HubSpot clean and up to date for accurate forecasting

What are we looking for?

  • Proven experience running a full outbound sales cycle, with a track record of closing high-volume SMB deals fast

  • A cold calling native - you're comfortable picking up the phone 50+ times a day and know how to hook a prospect in the first 30 seconds

  • SaaS sales experience is a must - you'll know what an API is and can hold your own in a conversation with a technical buyer

  • Consistent quota attainment and overachievement - we want to see the numbers, not just the narrative

  • Sharp, instinctive discovery skills - you can uncover pain quickly

  • Natural curiosity and hunger to become a product expert, so every conversation is relevant and consultative

  • You have experience and a great understanding of the DACH region.

  • Fluency in English; German is a plus.

  • Familiarity with HubSpot is a nice to have

About the Role
We're hiring Linkup's first SDR/BDR, a hybrid pipeline-generation role covering both sides of the funnel: qualifying inbound signups and running structured outbound into our priority segments (AI-native companies, GTM tooling providers, enterprise and regulated accounts).
You'll work closely with our VP Sales, picking accounts, drafting outbound, and partnering with AEs to turn interest into qualified pipeline. High ownership, fast feedback loop.

What You'll Do

  • Research target accounts and draft personalized multi-channel outreach (email, LinkedIn, phone) for founder-led and AE-assisted outbound

  • Monitor and pre-qualify inbound signups against our ICP (AI-native, GTM tooling, enterprise), then route to the right AE

  • Support first-touch qualification alongside AEs, learning our lead framework (ICP fit, pain, volume, timing, right entry point) as you go

  • Keep every touch logged in Attio

  • Help tune outbound messaging and channels as we scale campaigns across segments


Why This Role Matters
This is the first dedicated pipeline-generation hire at Linkup. Get it right and it compounds into every AE's quota.

You're a Great Fit If You

  • Have 0 to 2 years in SDR/BDR, or a first job out of a fast-paced, competitive environment (sales, consulting, we care about drive more than tenure)

  • Are comfortable with high-volume outbound and don't wait to be told what to do

  • Write clean, direct, non-generic outreach, no template-speak

  • Are curious about AI/agents and can hold a real conversation with a technical buyer, even without an engineering background

  • Want ownership fast, this role works closely with sales leadership, not layers of management

Our Stack
Attio (CRM), LemList (outbound), Slack, Notion, Apollo/Sales Navigator (prospecting), Snitcher (visitor ID), RB2B

About Linkup
Our Vision

We believe in a future of AI agents and the agentic web. These digital entities can create more value for humanity than we ever could alone, but they depend on the internet to operate, collaborate, take action, and gather information.

AI agents need web search. To perform well, they require information that is current, reliable, and context‑specific—not the diffuse, steadily aging knowledge frozen at their last training cut‑off.

Modern web search is built for humans, not AIs. Instead of trusted facts, it serves links, ads, and click‑bait. People want visually engaging pages; AI systems need structured truth. An AI can absorb oceans of data, while human attention barely skims the surface. Humans think visually and intuitively; AI reasons in latent space.

Web 2.0 is sunsetting. The deck is being reshuffled, and the Bing‑Google search oligopoly is crumbling. Indexing ever more pages is no longer the goal; semantically organizing facts for AI systems is. In the coming agentic web, Google’s ad‑driven model has no natural home.

Search for AI must be rebuilt from the ground up. We are reconstructing the web as a rigorously structured knowledge layer, mapping every concept, entity, and claim into a coherent semantic graph. This foundation delivers verified facts and rich context to AI instantly, unlocking faster reasoning, higher accuracy, and radically more useful answers for everyone.

Humans search Google; AI searches Linkup.

 

Our Mission

Reality never stands still, and neither should intelligence. Linkup reconnects language models to a living stream of verified facts, ensuring AIs remain as current and insightful as the world they serve.

Our mission is to deliver the world’s freshest, most trusted knowledge to AIs.

 

Our Culture

Our culture is built on the following values:

  • Mission. We believe we play a critical role in building the agentic web. We are 100% committed to our mission of bringing the reality of the world to AI agents.

  • Speed. We build fast, we build to last. We get things done, well.

  • Ownership. We empower every team member to take ownership of their projects, ensuring they see them through to successful completion.

  • Teamwork. Our strength lies in our unity. We rely on one another and embrace our diversity as a core asset.

  • Humility. We maintain low egos, showing respect for others and continuously learning from their insights and experiences.

We expect all team member to take an active role in shaping our company culture.

 

Our Team

We are small technical team, working shoulder to shoulder to build the web of agents.

A bit more about our 3 co-founders:

  • Philippe Mizrahi- Led the development of Lyft’s Autonomous Vehicles marketplace. Previously launched Amundsen, an open source search engine.

  • Denis Charrier- Founding Engineer at Niland, an audio search company (acquired by Spotify), then Staff Engineer at Spotify. 15y of software development experience.

  • Boris Toledano- Led robotics at Carrefour, after 3y at McKinsey & Co working on public affairs and digital transformation.

jobs.title: Aerothermal Engineer
jobs.description:
Aerothermal Engineer

About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

You will own the full thermal and aerothermal engineering cycle for our UAV platforms: from early design recommendations and simulation to wind tunnel experiments and flight test campaigns. Your work directly impacts the survivability, reliability, and performance of our systems in contested environments. You will be the technical authority on heat transfer, thermal management, and aerothermal interactions across all vehicle programs — working closely with aerodynamics, propulsion, mechanical, and GNC teams to ensure our platforms perform within thermal limits under real operational conditions.

Responsibilities

  • Aerothermal Design & Recommendations: Provide early-stage design guidance on thermal management architecture — including cooling inlet design, heat shield placement, exhaust routing, and surface coatings — to ensure airframes remain within thermal limits across the full flight envelope.

  • Thermal & Aerothermal Simulation: Set up, run, and validate lower fidelity thermal models, simulations and coupled thermal-fluid CFD tools (e.g., OpenFOAM). Model convective, conductive, and radiative heat transfer on internal components (batteries, motors, avionics) and external aerodynamic surfaces.

  • Design Optimization: Drive iterative aerothermal optimization cycles to minimize thermal drag penalty, reduce hotspot intensity, and maximize cooling efficiency. Leverage scripting and automated workflows to sweep design parameters and converge on optimal configurations.

  • Wind Tunnel Test Campaigns: Design, plan, and execute aerothermal wind tunnel experiments. Define instrumentation strategy (thermocouples, heat flux sensors, pressure taps), write test plans, operate test rigs, and lead post-test data analysis and correlation with simulation.

  • Flight Test Campaigns: Contribute to and lead in-flight thermal measurement campaigns. Define DAQ architecture for thermal sensors, develop test matrices, analyze flight data, and correlate with CFD predictions to validate models and sign off thermal margins.

  • Cross-functional Integration: Act as the thermal interface between the aerodynamics, propulsion, mechanical, and GNC teams — ensuring that thermal constraints are reflected in system-level trade-offs and that heat rejection requirements are accounted for in the airframe design.

Requirements

  • Education: B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field with a strong focus on fluid mechanics and heat transfer.

  • AeroThermal Fundamentals: Solid theoretical grounding in convective, conductive, and radiative heat transfer; boundary layer theory; and viscous flow physics as applied to aircraft surfaces and internal cooling passages.

  • Thermal Simulation Proficiency: Hands-on experience with CFD simulations in at least one major solver (OpenFOAM, Star-CCM+, ANSYS Fluent/CFX, or equivalent). Ability to select appropriate thermal boundary conditions, turbulence models, and mesh strategies for accuracy.

  • Experimental Testing: Demonstrated experience planning and executing thermal measurement campaigns — either in wind tunnel or in-flight — including instrumentation selection, DAQ setup, data reduction, and uncertainty analysis.

  • Python Proficiency: Ability to script data processing pipelines, automate post-processing of thermal simulation outputs, and interface with experimental DAQ systems.

  • Technical Communication: Ability to translate complex aerothermal findings into clear design recommendations for multidisciplinary teams.

Nice to have

  • General Aerodynamic Knowledge: Familiarity with the fundamentals of external aerodynamics — lift and drag generation, pressure distributions, boundary layer behaviour, and flow separation — as applied to fixed-wing or multirotor UAV platforms.

  • RC Knowledge: Hands-on experience building, flying, or tuning RC aircraft or drones — whether fixed-wing, quadcopter, or hybrid configurations.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

jobs.title: Senior Full Stack Product Engineer (TypeScript)
jobs.description:
Senior Full Stack Product Engineer (TypeScript)

About Maze

Maze is the user research platform that helps companies build the right products faster by making user insights available at the speed of product development.

In most companies, research demand far exceeds supply. Time, cost, and lack of access to expertise hold teams back. In today’s AI-powered world, anyone can build a product fast. The real challenge? Deeply understanding user needs and building the right product. That’s where Maze comes in.

We believe companies shouldn’t have to choose between building fast and building right. Maze makes research accessible, intuitive, and fast so product teams can put user insights at the center of every decision.

Our platform enables researchers, designers, and product managers to quickly recruit participants, run studies autonomously, and surface insights that actually drive product decisions. Our AI capabilities automate the busywork and add depth and direction to the insights themselves.

That’s why Maze was recently named the #1 user research platform in UX Tools’ Design Tools Survey—and why we’re scaling fast across industries like B2B SaaS, e-Commerce, Financial Services, Retail, and Automotive, supporting world class customers such as Uber, Amazon, Atlassian, Anthropic & more.

Maze is a Series B company backed by top-tier investors (Felicis, Emergence & Amplify). We operate a global remote workforce driven by our core values.

Location: Remote, preference for Netherlands, United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain or Portugal. Key engineering and product teams are based in these locales.

The Role

As a Senior Full Stack Software Engineer on the Product Engineering team, you'll design and deliver high impact features, working closely with product, design, and other engineers to solve complex problems, build scalable solutions, and ensure our systems are maintainable and performant.

You’ll take ownership of projects from concept to production, contribute to architectural decisions, write high quality code, and help raise the technical bar by sharing knowledge and best practices with your teammates.

You'll work on:

  • Building elegant features for user researchers to analyze and extract compelling insights from qualitative data, using both classical techniques and large language models

  • Expanding audience management to help researchers connect with and reward participants from across the world

  • Integrating video and scheduling tools to provide a streamlined experience for managing and booking user interviews

As a product engineer at Maze, you will:

  • Partner closely with product managers, designers and other engineers to design, build, and ship new features

  • Establish best practices, frameworks, and repeatable processes that enable us to measure the impact of every feature that we ship

  • Evaluate and improve the performance, maintainability, and security of applications in production

  • Work in a collaborative and open team, which places high value on feedback, continuous learning and trust.

You should apply if:

  • You're proficient with modern full-stack JavaScript (Node.js and React) and relational databases (PostgreSQL)

  • You're enthusiastic about well-tested code and strive to improve your work environment

  • You have excellent written and spoken English skills

  • You thrive in a remote environment

Bonus points:

  • You have Next.js, NestJS, GraphQL, and/or TypeScript experience

  • You have experience with AWS and/or Kubernetes

  • You're interested in UX, UI design, and the research field

Inclusivity and Pay

At Maze, we are dedicated to building an equitable, inclusive, and authentic workspace. Unique and diverse perspectives are welcomed, and continuous growth is encouraged. We believe that people are more than their resumes, so if your past experience looks different than the criteria listed, we'd still love to hear from you. We appreciate and celebrate non-traditional life routes and encourage you to apply should you connect with a job description or the Maze culture.

Maze values transparency and it enables us to approach compensation equitably across the world. We are informed by data and regularly check our salary ranges (either United States or Rest of World) against other venture backed companies. Additionally, we are proud of our holistic and generous benefits offerings, included in every compensation package.

Your salary is dependent upon many factors, including years of experience, expertise, etc. During your first interview, you can expect to have an open conversation with your recruiter regarding your compensation expectations.

Why Maze is unique

  • Early-stage startup: You will join an early-stage startup with less than 150 team members. This means you'll have the unique opportunity to directly impact success and help shape the future of Maze.

  • Market disruption: We believe that the way companies build products is fundamentally broken and the user research market is ripe for disruption. For too long, companies have been forced to choose between rapid development without user insights or investing months into research before bringing products to market. But there's finally a groundswell building around a path forward that eliminates this compromise - and Maze is leading the charge.

  • Product-market Fit: Maze is used by 100,000+ brands across 4,000 companies, from SMB to enterprises, and in the last fiscal year, we saw 6.5M questions answered, supporting 25K decisions

Benefits

  • Health insurance with international coverage, vision, and dental: 100% of the team member premium paid

    • For some locations, coverage options vary, please see our benefits pages for more information

  • Free access to proper mental health care, unlimited virtual therapy sessions (with a human) and 24/7 access to resources

  • Flexible time off

  • $1,500 remote work setup fund to ensure you can set up a productive work space

  • Flexible work schedule where you manage your own working hours

  • Virtual social engagements randomly throughout the year

  • SWAG, we have some really cool swag

  • Open, transparent culture that includes virtual: coffee chats, bi-weekly all-hands meetings, and more

Check out all of our a-maze-ing benefits here.

jobs.title: Program Director (m/f/d)
Founding Brand Manager (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Founding Brand Manager (m/w/d)
Über Aampere

Werde Teil von Aampere, einem Seed-Stage VC-backed Startup, das den europäischen Markt für gebrauchte E-Autos neu definiert. Seit unserem Launch ermöglichen wir EV-Besitzern einen schnellen & reibungslosen Verkauf innerhalb von 48h. Kaufende Händler aus ganz Europa haben Zugriff auf E-Autos von bisher nicht erschlossene Kundengruppen.

Unser Team kommt aus der deutschen Startup-Szene mit Erfahrung bei Autarc, Limehome, Cardino, Wemolo, Sixt, Porsche, Mercedes, Enterprise und Cazoo.


Deine Mission

Wir bauen bei Aampere gerade eine Marke von 0 auf. Bisher kommen über 95 % unserer Kunden aus Growth Marketing und unsere Brand Awareness bei EV-Fahrern liegt bei ca. 5 bis 10 %.
Da wir eine starke B2C-Brand aufbauen wollen, wissen wir, dass wir früh in Brand investieren müssen. Wer in Deutschland ein E-Auto verkaufen will, soll automatisch an Aampere denken und wir suchen die Person, die das für uns umsetzt.
Die Strategie legst du mit dem Head of Marketing fest. Die Umsetzung liegt komplett bei dir, ohne Micro-Management im Tagesgeschäft.

Du planst die Kampagnen und führst sie auch durch. Du entscheidest Umfang, Region, Kanäle und Botschaft, von OOH über YouTube bis PR und Community. Nichts ist vorentschieden. Du testest Regionen gegeneinander und skalierst, was gewinnt.
Du bestimmst, wofür Aampere steht. Aus Research zu Kunden, Markt und Wettbewerb entstehen Positionierung, Narrative und Tone of Voice. Das Fundament gibt es noch nicht, aber die Research dafür würde schon gestartet.
Du denkst über Awareness Kanäle hinaus. Ein großer Teil unserer Brand Wahrnehmung entsteht während des Sales Prozesses. Du denkst vom ersten bis zum letzten Touchpoint der Customer Journey und sorgst in den richtigen Momenten für die richtige Message & Erfahrung.
Du bekommst ein sechsstelliges Budget. Wir planen ein festes Budget für Brand in 2027 ein. Wohin wir es investieren, liegt komplett bei dir.


Das bringst du mit

Du hast eine Brand von null mitgebaut. 4 bis 6 Jahre Brand-Erfahrung im B2C, Startup oder startup-nah. Du hast nicht ein bereits bestehendes System verwaltet, sondern eines aufgebaut.
Du denkst von Konzept bis Go-Live. Du hast Multi-Channel-Kampagnen bereits selbst konzipiert und live gebracht. Du weißt genau, wann welcher Kanal der richtige ist und wie wir unsere Message gezielt an die Kunden übermitteln. Du musst dabei nicht jeden Schritt selbst ausführen, sondern kannst auch auf externe Ressourcen zurückgreifen.
Du hast kreative Ideen und verstehst, weshalb sie funktionieren. Wir suchen die Person, die auf Sachen kommt, an die im Growth-Team niemand denkt. Zeig uns eine Kampagne, die es ohne dich nicht gegeben hätte und was danach messbar anders war.
Du baust das Fundament, nicht nur die Maßnahmen. Gute Kampagnen entstehen nur durch eine gute Grundlage. Du weißt, wie man aus Research eine Brand-Identity baut und kannst sie genau erklären.
Du bist ein Operator. Du führst eigenständig Audits, Feldbefragungen und Kampagnen durch. Du wartest nicht auf Ansagen und brauchst niemanden, der dich steuert.
Du denkst in Ergebnissen. Uns ist bewusst, dass Brand nicht 100% messbar ist. Trotzdem erwarten wir Outcome-getriebenes Handeln. Du findest heraus, wie wir eine starke, wiedererkennbare Marke bauen und erst Deutschland und anschließend EU-weit distribuieren.
Du bist AI-native. Eigene, kreative Ideen sind uns extrem wichtig. Für die Umsetzung solltest du allerdings AI allerdings als Hebel nutzen können, um Ideen schneller auf die Straße zu bringen.
Deutsch ist deine Muttersprache. Unser B2C-Messaging findet zunächst in Deutschland statt. Gutes Englisch setzen wir voraus.


Why Aampere?

Startup Umfeld: jeden Tag etwas bewirken und gemeinsam mit uns die Welt elektrisieren
Persönliches Wachstum: Im schnelllebigen Umfeld kannst du schnell aufsteigen und Verantwortung übernehmen
Tech: Ob Apple oder Windows, dein Laptop wird von uns gestellt. Du entscheidest, womit du am besten arbeitest.
Urban Sports Club und 58€ Ticket: healthy team, happy team
Late Dinner im Office: Wenn es abends länger wird, übernehmen wir dein Dinner (Uber Eats)
Offsite: bis jetzt waren wir am Lago Maggiore, in den Alpen und am Tegernsee, what’s next?
Wohnen im Werksviertel: Im naheliegenden Co-Living Space gibt es die Möglichkeit, eigenständig ein Zimmer zu mieten - mit Blick auf das Riesenrad. 


Aampere ist nichts für dich wenn...

...du überwiegend remote arbeiten willst. Wir glauben, dass die besten Ideen entstehen, wenn Menschen im selben Raum sind. Deshalb bist du mindestens vier Tage pro Woche bei uns im Office.

...du fertige Prozesse und Strukturen vorfinden willst. Bei uns gibt es vieles davon noch nicht. Wir suchen Leute, die Strukturen und Prozesse selbst bauen, statt sie zu verwalten.

...du einen fertigen Plan brauchst, bevor du loslegst. Seed Stage heißt: vieles ist unklar und ändert sich wöchentlich. Du musst dich wohl damit fühlen, im Ungewissen zu entscheiden und unterwegs zu korrigieren.

...du in deiner Lane bleiben willst. "Das ist nicht mein Job" kennen wir nicht. Du packst da an, wo es brennt, auch wenn es außerhalb deiner Rollenbeschreibung liegt.

...du einen klassischen 9-to-5-Job willst. Wir bauen etwas Großes und das geht nicht nebenbei. Wer hier ist, will Vollgas geben, statt nur die Zeit abzusitzen.


Wie wir arbeiten

Drei Werte, keine Poster an der Wand, sondern wie wir täglich arbeiten, einstellen und wachsen:

Aaudacity. Wir sind mutig genug, Risiken einzugehen, und schnell genug, es nicht halbherzig zu tun.
Aambition to grow. Wir wollen wachsen, als Menschen und als Unternehmen.
Aampact over Hierarchy. Die beste Idee gewinnt, egal von wem sie kommt. Titel entscheiden hier keine Diskussion.


Noch ein paar Worte zum Abschluss

Bewirb dich jetzt! Wir freuen uns über Deine formlose Bewerbung - alles weitere besprechen wir gemeinsam.

Egal, welchen Hintergrund, welche Herkunft oder welche Geschlechtsidentität du mitbringst – bei uns zählt, wer du als Person bist. Wir fördern eine Kultur des Respekts und Miteinanders, in der jede Stimme gehört wird, persönliche Weiterentwicklung möglich ist und Wertschätzung an erster Stelle steht.

Senior Solutions Architect - Data & AI Engineer (f/m/d, 4-Days-Week), German Speaking
It’s time to change. We change!

Über uns
It’s time to change. We change! Willkommen bei Auvaria, wo Leidenschaft, Teamgeist und Verantwortung unsere Kultur prägen. Wir sind ein mehrfach ausgezeichneter AWS Consulting & Engineering Partner mit Büros in Wien, Hamburg und Belgrad und begleiten unsere Kunden als Trusted Advisor auf der gesamten Cloud Journey.

Über die Rolle
Was auch immer unsere Kunden im Bereich Data & AI auf AWS vorhaben, wir entwerfen und entwickeln es gemeinsam vom ersten Architecture Workshop bis in Production mit ihnen. Dafür suchen wir dich: als Senior Solutions Architect für Data & AI verantwortest du End-to-End Projekte in deinem Bereich und gestaltest unsere wachsende Data & AI Business Unit aktiv mit.

Architektur & Delivery 

  • Du führst die Entwicklung und Implementierung skalierbare AWS-Architekturen für Data Platforms und Gen AI- / Agentic AI-Lösungen

SAP Account Executive (m/w/d)
Deine Aufgaben

Du weißt, dass du zu den Besten gehörst.  Dein Umfeld weiß es auch.  Aber deine aktuelle Rolle gibt dir nicht mehr den Raum, den du verdienst.   Du hast in den letzten Jahren Deals geschlossen, die andere für unmöglich hielten. Du kennst das SAP-Ökosystem nicht aus Präsentationen – sondern aus echten Co-Sell-Gesprächen, aus Partnerverhandlungen, aus Abschlüssen, die du persönlich über die Linie gebracht hast.  Jetzt fragst du dich: Gibt es eine Rolle, die meinem Anspruch wirklich gerecht wird?   Die gibt es. Und du liest sie gerade. 

Die Rolle

 Dies ist eine reine New-Business-Position mit klarer strategischer Bedeutung für Implicos Wachstum in SAP-zentrierten Prozessindustrien. Du verantwortest die Gewinnung neuer Kundenlogos in den Segmenten Landwirtschaft, Bergbau, Chemie sowie Zement und Baustoffe – in enger Co-Sell-Partnerschaft mit SAP Account Teams und Industry Business Units.  Du bewegst dich in einem Umfeld, in dem Vertrauen, Substanz und Marktkenntnisse entscheiden – nicht Lautstärke. 
 
Deine Verantwortung

  • Vollständige Quota-Verantwortung für neues ARR aus Prozessindustrie-Kunden
  • Identifikation und Qualifizierung von Opportunities aus der SAP-ADRM-Pipeline sowie dem eigenen Netzwerk
  • Aufbau und Pflege belastbarer Co-Sell-Beziehungen mit SAP SCM Sales Reps und IBU-Kontakten
  • Steuerung komplexer Sales-Zyklen von 3–9 Monaten mit mehreren Entscheidungsträgern auf IT-, Operations- und C-Level-Ebene
  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Solution Architects für technische Deep Dives und Proof-of-Value-Definitionen
  • Akkurate Pipeline-Führung im CRM sowie strukturiertes Forecasting
  • Kontinuierliche Rückmeldung von Markt- und Wettbewerbsinformationen an Product- und GTM-Teams


Dein Profil

Was wir voraussetzen:
